subject: CPFTA Rules of Origin Regulations
precis: Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement Rules of Origin Regulations (CPFTA) implement, in Canada, the rules of origin negotiated by Canada and Peru, which will be used to determine when goods have undergone sufficient production to qualify for preferential tariff treatment under the CPFTA.  Preferential tariff treatment under the CPFTA, which reflects the actual reduction in specific rates of duty, has been implemented in the Customs Tariff through Bill C-24.

subject: CPFTA Rules of Origin for Casual Goods Regulations
precis: Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement Rules of Origin for Casual Goods Regulations (CPFTA) set out the origin requirements for low-value shipments and for goods imported by travelers to ensure that eligible goods qualify without onerous documentation requirements.

subject: CPFTA Tariff Preference Regulations
precis: Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement Tariff Preference Regulations (CPFTA) allow eligible goods that are not shipped directly between Peru and Canada to retain their eligibility for preferential tariff rates provided that they remain under customs control in third countries.

subject: CPFTA Sugar Aggregate Quantity Limit Order
precis: CANADA-PERU FREE TRADE AGREEMENT SUGAR AGGREGATE QUANTITY LIMIT ORDER (CPFTA) sets out annual quantities of refined sugar imported from Peru that could benefit from the preferential rate under the CPFTA.

subject: Companies’ Creditors Arrangement Regulations

subject: Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport Zoning Regulations

precis: REGULATIONS AMENDING THE LETTER MAIL REGULATIONS, effective January 11, 2010, which establish the domestic basic letter rate – the rate for sending a letter weighing 30 g or less anywhere in Canada - for the next five years. act: Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act
subject: Canada Oil and Gas Drilling and Production Regulations
precis: CANADA OIL AND GAS DRILLING AND PRODUCTION REGULATIONS in order to amalgamate and modernize the existing Drilling Regulations and the Production and Conservation Regulations that currently exist, in mirror form, under the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act and the Accord Acts.  The new regulations address the high level of duplication between the existing regulations and increasing requests to use new or cost effective technologies and processes not reflected in the current regulations.

subject: Newfoundland Offshore Petroleum Drilling and Production Regulations

The regulations include requiring the reporting of operating and capital expenditures, including the cost of well operation, in operators' Annual Production Reports.  This ensures that the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Petroleum Board receives the information necessary for regulatory oversight to ensure appropriate production and management of the resource in order to prevent waste, as well as to verify whether the operator is in compliance with section 65 of the provincial regulations.

subject: Order Fixing March 26, 2010 as the Date of the Coming into Force of Certain Sections of the Act

subject: Regulations Amending the Regulations Excluding Certain Indictable Offences from the Definition of¨"Designated Offence"
precis: Regulations Amending the REGULATIONS EXCLUDING CERTAIN INDICTABLE OFFENCES FROM THE DEFINITION OF 'DESIGNATED OFFENCE' by removing the Copyright Act from the list of statutes that are excluded from the definition of “designated offence” in relation to the application of the “proceeds of crime” provisions of the Criminal Code in order to allow such proceeds to fall within the ambit of the Criminal Code’s proceeds of crime regime.  This will improve the ability of law enforcement agencies to enforce the Copyright Act by permitting the seizure, restraint and confiscation of proceeds derived from the commission of copyright-related offences and will complement existing enforcement strategies to combat organized crime and copyright piracy.

precis: RENEWABLE FUELS REGULATIONS in order to reduce Greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions by mandating an average five percent renewable fuel content based on the gasoline volume, thereby contributing towards the protection of Canadians and the environment from the impacts of climate change.  The proposed Regulations are estimated to result in an incremental reduction of GHG emissions of about one Mt CO2e per year over and above the reductions attributable to existing provincial requirements already in place.  The propsed Regulations fulfill the commitments under the Renewable Fuels Strategy of reducing GHG emissions from liquid petroleum fuels and create a demand for renewable fuels in Canada.

subject: Regulations Amending the Food and Drug Regulations (1319 - New Drugs for Extraordinary Use)

subject: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the IMMIGRATION AND REFUGEE PROTECTION REGULATIONS, in order to ensure that the wording in the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations is consistent with Bill C-35 – which is now coming into force. Applications must now include information about persons who represented or have advised the applicant for consideration at any stage leading up to the formal application or proceeding

subject: CCOFTA Rules of Origin Regulations

subject: Regulations Amending the Health of Animals Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the HEALTH OF ANIMALS REGULATIONS in order to (1) reduce the impacts of a disease outbreak, or food safety issue resulting from or affecting the pig sector; (2) better protect public health and animal health; and (3) support the Canadian pork industry in order to meet international standards to export.

subject: Regulations Amending the Pest Control Products Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending THE PEST CONTROL PRODUCT REGULATIONS in order to provide Canadian agriculture producers with access to an import mechanism that (1) mitigates unacceptable health and environmental risks from imported foreign products; (2) balances the interests of growers and product registrants by promoting price discipline in the Canadian pesticide marketplace while respecting registrants’ investments in Canadian product registration; (3) is aligned with other instruments aimed at enhancing competition for agricultural production input; and (4) makes administrative corrections and addresses inconsistencies between the French and English versions of the Regulations.

subject: Regulations Amending the Radiation Emitting Devices Regulations (Tanning Equipment)
precis: Regulations Amending the RADIATION EMITTING DEVICES REGULATIONS (TANNING EQUIPMENT) in order to provide users of tanning equipment with clear information on the risks of using tanning equipment. Updating the health risk information on tanning equipment warning labels will respond to scientific findings that tanning equipment users are at an increased risk of developing skin cancer, and youth are at an even greater risk.

subject: Rules Amending Certain Rules Made under the Tax Court of Canada Act
precis: RULES AMENDING CERTAIN RULES MADE UNDER THE TAX COURT OF CANADA ACT in order to (1) streamline the process of hearings and codifying the practice relating to litigation process conferences; (2) implement new rules and amend existing rules governing expert witnesses and their evidence in the Tax Court of Canada; (3) allow the Court to proceed with a hearing of two or more appeals, while others are stayed pending a decision on the appeals heard by the Court; (4) encourage parties to settle their dispute early in the litigation process; (5) add a rule indicating when judgments are pronounced and deposited with the Registry; and (6) make technical amendments to the Rules.

subject: Regulations Amending the Atlantic Pilotage Tariff Regulations, 1996

subject: Order Amending the Schedule to the Tobacco Act
precis: Order Amending the SCHEDULE TO THE TOBACCO ACT in order to (1) protect young persons from inducements to use tobacco products by further limiting the availability of flavoured cigar types that are attractive to youth; and (2) remove the ability of the tobacco industry to market most flavoured cigars in Canada.

subject: Regulations Amending the Canadian Aviation Regulations (Parts l, Vl and Vll — Flight Attendants and Emergency Evacuation)
precis: Regulations Amending the CANADIAN AVIATION REGULATIONS (PARTS I, VI AND VII - FLIGHT ATTENDANTS AND EMERGENCY EVACUATION) in order to (1) provide Subpart 705 operators with the option to use either flight attendant ratio (i.e., the 1:40 passengers or the 1:50 passenger seats flight attendant ratio); (2) harmonize Subpart 604 operators flight attendant ratio with those of the United States to operate under the 1:50 passenger ratio for all models; and (3) address regulatory gaps by introducing the conditions under which an operator can utilize the 1:50 flight attendant ratio (i.e., incorporate the “mitigation features” into the regulatory text).

subject: Regulations Amending the Employment Insurance Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the EMPLOYMENT INSURANCE REGULATIONS in order to ensure that Employment Insurance (EI) claimants are treated fairly and consistently, whether they receive their pension as a lump sum or an annuity; and, to ensure the continued transparency of the EI premium rate for residents of Quebec and their employers.

subject: Regulations Amending the Citizenship Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the CITIZENSHIP REGULATIONS in order to support the implementation of the remaining provisions of the Strengthening Canadian Citizenship Act (SCCA) which include: (1) provisions relating to information sharing; (2) provisions relating to “lost Canadians” and grants of citizenship for adopted persons; (3) provisions relating to accompanying persons at hearings with citizenship judges; (4) technical amendments recommended by the Standing Joint Committee for the Scrutiny of Regulations; and (5) provisions relating to newenabling authorities granted in the SCCA.

subject: Canadian Payments Association Reporting Requirements Regulations
precis: CANADIAN PAYMENTS ASSOCIATION REPORTING REQUIREMENTS REGULATIONS in order to support the new accountability framework for the Canadian Payments Association by providing direction on preparing and submitting the corporate plan and annual report.

subject: Canadian Payments Association Election of Directors Regulations
precis: CANADIAN PAYMENTS ASSOCIATION ELECTION OF DIRECTORS REGULATIONS in order to (1) facilitate independent decision-making by the Canadian Payments Association (CPA) Board by setting criteria for determining if independent directors are free of conflict of interest with CPA members; (2) ensure that the largest users and contributors to CPA systems are represented in a balanced manner on the CPA Board; (3) provide guidelines for the selection of nominees for Director positions; and (4) remove outdated regulations that are no longer applicable given the new voting structure and Board composition imposed through the legislative amendments.

subject: Regulations Amending the Narcotic Control Regulations and the Marihuana for Medical Purposes Regulations (Communication of Information)

subject: Regulations Amending the Queen's Regulations and Orders for the Canadian Forces

subject: Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations, 2015

subject: Policy Committees, Work Place Committees and Health and Safety Representatives Regulations
precis:
POLICY COMMITTEES, WORK PLACE COMMITTEES AND HEALTH AND SAFETY REPRESENTATIVES REGULATIONS in order to (1) reduce accidents, illnesses and fatalities in federally regulated work places by improving the capacity of policy committees, work place committees and health and safety representatives to identify and address hazards in the work place; (2) harmonize the Regulations with the Canada Labour Code; (3) provide more direction on administrative procedures and requirements regarding the policy committees, work place committees and health and safety representatives; and (4) ensure the Regulations are up to date with the current practices and procedures in other jurisdictions.

.

subject: Regulations Amending the Territorial Quarrying Regulations

subject: Regulations Amending the Territorial Land Use Regulations

subject: National Energy Board Pipeline Damage Prevention Regulations - Obligations of Pipeline Companies

subject: Regulations Amending the Canada Grain Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the CANADA GRAIN REGULATIONS in order to (1) limit the accumulation of additional surplus in the Canada Grain Commission revolving fund related to official inspection and official weighing fees; (2) update the fees to reflect the costs of providing official inspection and official weighing services; and (3) reduce the transactional burden of tracking and billing for official inspection overtime costs.

subject: Regulations Amending the Canada Student Financial Assistance Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the CANADA STUDENT FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE REGULATIONS in order to introduce the new national progressive eligibility thresholds for Canada Student Grant for Full-Time Students to ensure that more students benefit from up-front, non-repayable student financial assistance each year.

subject: Regulations Amending the General Preferential Tariff and Least Developed Country Tariff Rules of Origin Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the GENERAL PREFERENTIAL TARIFF AND LEAST DEVELOPED COUNTRY TARIFF RULES OF ORIGIN REGULATIONS in order to implement the Budget 2017 initiative to improve market access for least developed countries by allowing them to use manufacturing inputs sourced from, and processed in, an expanded list of countries in the production of T-shirts and pants that qualify for duty-free importation into Canada.

subject: Regulations Amending the Metal Mining Effluent Regulations

subject: Regulations Amending the Metal Mining Effluent Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the METAL MINING EFFLUENT REGULATIONS in order to enable the deposit of mine waste in four fish-frequented water bodies at the BlackRock Mining Project.

subject: Order Amending Schedule 1 to the Species at Risk Act

subject: Regulations Amending the Canada Student Financial Assistance Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the CANADA STUDENT FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE REGULATIONS (CSFAR) in order to (1) amend the income thresholds in Table 1 and Table 2 set out in Schedule 3 to the CSFAR to account for the annual growth in the relevant provincial/territorial Consumer Price Index, and allow the eligibility for the Canada Students Grants and Part-Time Canada Student Loans tied to Schedule 3 to continue to reflect the students’ real family income; and (2) remove the discretion in subsection 24(1) by setting out the instances when the Minister shall cancel and reduce the repayment assistance that was granted as a result of an error by the borrower in their Repayment Assistance Plan application.

subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Canada Labour Code
precis: Regulations Amending CERTAIN REGULATIONS MADE UNDER THE CANADA LABOUR CODE in order to (1) protect the health of employees in the federal jurisdiction and provide regulatory certainty by setting appropriate Occupational Exposure Limit for airborne asbestos fibre; (2) ensure consistency with most provincial and territorial regulatory regimes for airborne asbestos fibre; (3) protect the health of employees in the federal jurisdiction by regulating work activities such as handling, removal, repair or disturbance of asbestos-containing materials that could expose employees to friable asbestos; and (4) ensure that the Government of Canada is in compliance with the Asbestos Convention, 1986 (No. 162).

subject: Regulations Amending the Food and Drug Regulations (Importation of Drugs for an Urgent Public Health Need)

subject: P.C. 2017-60 of January 25, 2017 ** AMENDMENT **

subject: Ambassador Bridge Enhancement Project

act: Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement Implementation Act
subject: Order Fixing September 21, 2017 as the Day on which the Act Comes into Force, other than Certain Provisions
precis: Order fixing September 21, 2017 as the day on which the CANADA–EUROPEAN UNION COMPREHENSIVE ECONOMIC AND TRADE AGREEMENT IMPLEMENTATION ACT, chapter 6 of the Statutes of Canada, 2017 COMES INTO FORCE, other than subsection 8(3), paragraph 11(1)(a), subsection 11(2), paragraph 13(a) and sections 45 to 58, 90, and 133 to 137.

subject: Certificate of Supplementary Protection Regulations
precis: CERTIFICATE OF SUPPLEMENTARY PROTECTION REGULATIONS in order to establish the Certificates of Supplementary Protection regime which implements Canada's commitment in the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement by providing for an additional period of patent-like protection for drugs containing a new medicinal ingredient, or a new combination of medicinal ingredients.

subject: Regulations Amending the Patented Medicines (Notice of Compliance) Regulations, 2017
precis: Regulations Amending the PATENTED MEDICINES (NOTICE OF COMPLIANCE) REGULATIONS in order to (1) resolve a number of problems by replacing summary prohibition proceedings with full actions to determine patent validity and infringement; (2) expand the scope of the Regulations to cover relevant certificates of supplementary protection, by providing an additional period of protection for new patented pharmaceutical products; (3) expedite proceedings by introducing a limited number of procedural rules, while still leaving the Court broad discretion to manage proceedings; 4) address concerns about how damages arising from delayed generic market entry are currently assessed; and 5) remove barriers that may prevent innovators and generics from litigating certain patents outside the Regulations prior to generic market entry.

subject: Rules Amending the Patent Rules
precis: RULES AMENDING THE PATENT RULES in order to remove the references to representatives appointed under section 29 of the Patent Act, as that section is repealed with the coming into force of the Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement Implementation Act.

subject: Regulations Amending the Investment Canada Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the INVESTMENT CANADA REGULATIONS so that Non-Canadians to which the $1.5 billion in enterprise value net  benefit review threshold applies are able to calculate the value of the Canadian business being acquired in order to meet Canada's commitments in the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement.

subject: Regulations Amending the Pest Control Products Regulations (Test Data Protection)
precis: Regulations Amending the PEST CONTROL PRODUCTS REGULATIONS (TEST DATA PROTECTION) in order to align the Regulations with the amendments to the Act in order to meet the CANADA-EUROPEAN UNION COMPREHENSIVE ECONOMIC AND TRADE AGREEMENT commitment to avoid duplicative animal testing.

subject: Regulations Specifying Territories and Indicating International Registers
precis: REGULATIONS SPECIFYING TERRITORIES AND INDICATING INTERNATIONAL REGISTERS in order to specify those territories not referred to in the definition of “territory of the European Union” and to indicate those registers that are international registers, for the purposes of applying the Coasting Trade Act.

subject: Order Amending the Import Control List
precis: Order Amending the IMPORT CONTROL LIST (ICL) in order to (1) amend the ICL in order to add Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement import Origin Quotas-eligible goods to the ICL; (2) remove imports controls for certain beef and veal, as well as milk protein substances; and 3) update the Harmonized System codes or descriptions for certain ICL items.

subject: Order Amending the Export Control List
precis: Order Amending the EXPORT CONTROL LIST in order to add certain Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) export Origin Quota-eligible goods to the Export Control List in order for the Government of Canada to establish export permit requirements for these goods.

subject: Export Allocations Regulations
precis: EXPORT ALLOCATIONS REGULATIONS in order to administer certain Origin Quotas through the issuance of export allocations and export permits by prescribing the information to be provided in an application for an allocation.

subject: Export Permits Regulations (Non-strategic Products)
precis: EXPORT PERMITS REGULATIONS (NON-STRATEGIC PRODUCTS) in order to require information from applicants for export permits for non-strategic goods, including Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement Origin Quota goods, similar to the Export Permit Regulations and the Import Permit Regulations, but with small differences to account for the nature of non-strategic goods (i.e. high-sugar-containing products and vehicles).

subject: CETA Rules of Origin Regulations
precis: CETA RULES OF ORIGIN REGULATIONS in order to fully implement Canada's tariff commitments under the CANADA-EUROPEAN UNION (EU) COMPREHENSIVE ECONOMIC AND TRADE AGREEMENT so that Canada and EU can proceed with implementation of the AGREEMENT.

subject: CETA Rules of Origin for Casual Goods Regulations
precis: CETA RULES OF ORIGIN FOR CASUAL GOODS REGULATIONS in order to fully implement Canada's tariff commitments under the CANADA-EUROPEAN UNION (EU) COMPREHENSIVE ECONOMIC AND TRADE AGREEMENT so that Canada and EU can proceed with implementation of the AGREEMENT.

subject: CETA Tariff Preference Regulations
precis: CETA TARIFF PREFERENCE REGULATIONS in order to fully implement Canada's tariff commitments under the CANADA-EUROPEAN UNION (EU) COMPREHENSIVE ECONOMIC AND TRADE AGREEMENT so that Canada and EU can proceed with implementation of the AGREEMENT.

subject: Regulations Defining "EU country or other CETA beneficiary"
precis: Regulations Defining "EU COUNTRY OR OTHER CETA BENEFICIARY" in order to fully implement Canada's tariff commitments under the CANADA-EUROPEAN UNION (EU) COMPREHENSIVE ECONOMIC AND TRADE AGREEMENT so that Canada and EU can proceed with implementation of the AGREEMENT.

subject: Order Amending the Schedule to the Customs Tariff (Extension of the Canada-European Union Tariff)
precis: Order Amending the SCHEDULE TO THE CUSTOMS TARIFF (EXTENSION OF THE CANADA-EUROPEAN UNION TARIFF) in order to fully implement Canada's tariff commitments under the CANADA-EUROPEAN UNION (EU) COMPREHENSIVE ECONOMIC AND TRADE AGREEMENT so that Canada and EU can proceed with implementation of the AGREEMENT.

subject: Regulations Amending the Vessel Duties Reduction or Removal Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the VESSEL DUTIES REDUCTION OR REMOVAL REGULATIONS in order to ensure that the Regulations reflect the changes being made to the COASTING TRADE ACT that implement the marine sector commitments of Canada under CANADA-EUROPEAN UNION COMPREHENSIVE ECONOMIC AND TRADE AGREEMENT.

subject: Regulations Amending the Canadian International Trade Tribunal Procurement Inquiry Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the CANADIAN INTERNATIONAL TRADE TRIBUNAL PROCUREMENT INQUIRY REGULATIONS in order to fully implement Canada's obligations under the CANADA-EUROPEAN UNION COMPREHENSIVE ECONOMIC AND TRADE AGREEMENT (CETA) in relation to procurement.

subject: Regulations Amending the Export Permits Regulations
precis: REGULATIONS AMENDING THE EXPORT PERMITS REGULATIONS in order to exclude from its scope the goods that will be subject to the new Export Permits Regulations (Non-Strategic Products) by the date of Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement’s provisional application.

subject: Regulations Amending the Ontario Fishery Regulations, 2007
precis: Regulations Amending the ONTARIO FISHERY REGULATIONS, 2007 in order to apply the differential daily catch and retain limit for non-residents currently in place in the Border Waters Area for sauger, wallleye, and lake trout throughout Fiisheries Management Zone 5 (i.e. sauger and walleye daily limit of 2; lake trout daily limit of 1).

subject: Regulations Amending the Off-Road Small Spark-Ignition Engine Emission Regulations and Making a Consequential Amendment to Another Regulation
precis: Regulations Amending the OFF-ROAD SMALL SPARK-IGNITION ENGINE EMISSION REGULATIONS AND MAKING A CONSEQUENTIAL AMENDMENT TO ANOTHER REGULATION in order to (1) reduce smog caused by air pollutant emissions from small spark-ignition (SSI) engines, which has a significant adverse impact on the health and environment of Canadians and, as a result, on the Canadian economy; and (2) restore common Canada U.S. standards for air pollutant emissions from SSI engines, and contribute to minimizing the administrative burden costs incurred by companies importing these engines into Canada.

subject: Regulations Amending the Metal Mining Effluent Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the METAL MINING EFFLUENT REGULATIONS in order to enable the deposit of mine waste in three fish-frequented water bodies at the Rainy River Mine.

subject: Regulations Amending the Weights and Measures Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the WEIGHTS AND MEASURES REGULATIONS in order to (1) make the regulatory text that prescribes the period in which traders must cause their device to be examined more coherent and easier to understand; and (2) prevent any confusion that implementation-specific dates and scenarios would have caused if kept in the text.

subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Nuclear Safety and Control Act
precis: Regulations Amending CERTAIN REGULATIONS MADE UNDER THE NUCLEAR SAFETY AND CONTROL ACT in order to (1) update and clarify existing requirements for radiation protection during an emergency with current international standards and practices; (2) ensure that human performance and fitness for duty are addressed by licensees of Class I nuclear facilities to support workers in conducting their daily tasks and to be prepared to effectively respond to nuclear emergencies; (3) ensure that nuclear power plant licensees undertake regular reviews against modern codes and standards to identify safety improvements to their facilities to ensure their continued safe operation; (4) modernize the Class I Nuclear Facilities Regulations and the Uranium Mines and Mills Regulations to reflect the nuclear industry’s best practice of placing paramount focus on safety through the implementation of a management system; and (5) update the Administrative Monetary Penalties Regulations (Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission) to reflect the amendments to the Radiation Protection Regulations.

subject: John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport Zoning Regulations
precis: JOHN C. MUNRO HAMILTON INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT ZONING REGULATIONS in order to limit the height of new buildings, structures, and objects, including trees, or any additions to existing buildings, structures, and objects on lands adjacent to or in the vicinity of the John C. Munro Hamilton International Airport.

subject: Montréal — Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport Zoning Regulations
precis: MONTRÉAL—PIERRE ELLIOTT TRUDEAU INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT ZONING REGULATIONS in order to (1) ensure that lands adjacent and in proximity to airports is used in a manner that is compatible with the safe operation of aircraft and of the airport; and (2) ensure that potential and future development surrounding the airport remains compatible with the safe operation of aircraft and of the airport.

act: Transportation Appeal Tribunal of Canada Act
subject: Rules Amending the Civil Aviation Tribunal Rules
precis: Rules Amending the CIVIL AVIATION TRIBUNAL RULES in order to reference relevant enactments and refer to determinations as well as decisions of the Transportation Appeal Tribunal of Canada Rules.

subject: Cap Tourmente National Wildlife Area ** Acquisition of lands **

subject: Eagle Village First Nation - Kipawa Indian Reserve ** Confirmation **

The lands are contiguous to the main site of the reserve which is located in the Abitibi-Témiscamingue federal district, 10 kilometres west of Témiscaming on Lake Kipawa, in Quebec.

subject: Special Economic Measures (Venezuela) Regulations

precis: Regulations Amending the GREAT LAKES PILOTAGE TARIFF REGULATIONS in order to enable the Authority to operate on a self-sustaining financial basis, with fair and reasonable tariffs that can support efficient pilotage services and ensure safe navigation.

subject: Regulations Amending the Pacific Pilotage Tariff Regulations

subject: Regulations Amending the Quebec Fishery Regulations, 1990
precis: Regulations Amending the QUEBEC FISHERY REGULATIONS, 1990 in order to (1) improve the regulatory management tools applied to Quebec’s Atlantic salmon sport fishery to better manage the fishery as the species population fluctuates and to facilitate the recruitment of new Atlantic salmon fishers to generate greater economic benefits; and (2) improve consistency between the Quebec Fishery Regulations (QFR), 1990 and Quebec’s Regulation respecting aquaculture and the sale of fish (RASF) with regard to bait fishing by adding to the QFR, 1990 certain species of fish prohibited for use as bait in Quebec’s RASF.

subject: Bank Recapitalization (Bail-in) Conversion Regulations
precis: BANK RECAPITALIZATION (BAIL-IN) CONVERSION REGULATIONS in order to (1) preserve financial stability by empowering the Governor in Council and Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation to quickly restore a failed systemically important bank to viability and allow it to remain open and operating, even where the bank has experienced severe losses; (2) reduce government and taxpayer exposure in the unlikely event of a failure of a systemically important bank; and (3) reduce the likelihood of a failure of a systemically important bank and increase market discipline by reinforcing that bank shareholders and creditors are responsible for the bank’s risks—not taxpayers.

subject: Bank Recapitalization (Bail-in) Issuance Regulations
precis: BANK RECAPITALIZATION (BAIL-IN) ISSUANCE REGULATIONS in order to (1) preserve financial stability by empowering the Governor in Council and Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation to quickly restore a failed systemically important bank to viability and allow it to remain open and operating, even where the bank has experienced severe losses; (2) reduce government and taxpayer exposure in the unlikely event of a failure of a systemically important bank; and (3) reduce the likelihood of a failure of a systemically important bank and increase market discipline by reinforcing that bank shareholders and creditors are responsible for the bank’s risks—not taxpayers.

subject: Compensation Regulations
precis: COMPENSATION REGULATIONS in order to (1) preserve financial stability by empowering the Governor in Council and Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation to quickly restore a failed systemically important bank to viability and allow it to remain open and operating, even where the bank has experienced severe losses; (2) reduce government and taxpayer exposure in the unlikely event of a failure of a systemically important bank; and (3) reduce the likelihood of a failure of a systemically important bank and increase market discipline by reinforcing that bank shareholders and creditors are responsible for the bank’s risks—not taxpayers.

subject: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations

subject: Regulations Amending Various GST/HST Regulations, No. 11

subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the United Nations Act

subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Special Economic Measures Act

subject: Regulations Amending the Special Economic Measures (Russia) Regulations

subject: Regulations Amending the Canadian Aviation Regulations (Parts I and VI – Flight Data Recorder and Cockpit Voice Recorder)
precis: Regulations Amending the CANADIAN AVIATION REGULATIONS (PARTS I AND VI – FLIGHT DATA RECORDER AND COCKPIT VOICE RECORDER) in order to (1) enhance the time period capture of Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) information, by extending the recording time from 30 minutes to two hours for those aircraft manufactured before 2003; (2) ensure the continued function of the CVR system in the case of a total aircraft power failure by requiring the use of a Recorder Independent Power Supply that will last for a 10-minute period for those aircraft manufactured after 2002 and already required to have a two hour CVR; (3) fully implement the International Civil Aviation Organization standards with respect to CVR and to align the Canadian Aviation Regulations with the United States Federal Aviation Administration standards in Title 14 of the United States Code of Federal Regulations. The amendments will capture all Canadian in-service aeroplanes over 5,700 kg and transport helicopters over 7,000 kg; and (4) clarify that a CVR is required anytime a multi-engine turbine powered aircraft capable of carrying six passengers or more is operated by two pilots.

Approval of the appointment by the Minister of Public Works and Government Services of JOCELYNE MARIE-PAULINE HOULE of Val-des-Bois, Quebec, to be Chairperson of the board of directors of Canada Lands Company Limited, to hold office during pleasure for a term of two years.

Approval of the appointment by the Minister of Public Works and Government Services of MARGARET FRANCES MACDONALD of Dartmouth, Nova Scotia, to be a director of the board of directors of Canada Lands Company Limited, to hold office during pleasure for a term of four years, in the place of Jocelyne Marie-Pauline Houle.

Approval of the appointment by the Minister of Canadian Heritage of HEATHER HOLDEN of Vancouver, British Columbia, to be a trustee of the Board of Trustees of the Canadian Museum of Nature, to hold office during pleasure for a term of three years, in the place of Alice McCarron, whose term has expired.

Approval of the appointment by the Minister of Canadian Heritage of CAROLINE LAJOIE of Québec, Quebec, to be a member of the Board of Directors of the National Capital Commission, to hold office during pleasure for a term of four years, effective July 1, 2019, in the place of Carol Loughrey, whose term will expire.

Approval of the re-appointment by the Minister of Canadian Heritage of LISA M. MACDONALD of New Glasgow, Nova Scotia, as a member of the Board of Directors of the National Capital Commission, to hold office during pleasure for a term of three years, effective July 1, 2019.

Approval of the appointment by the Minister of Canadian Heritage of LISE BERNIER of Saguenay, Quebec, to be a member of the Board of Directors of the National Capital Commission, to hold office during pleasure for a term of four years, effective June 22, 2019, in the place of Basil Stewart, whose term will expire.
Appointment of STEPHEN D. MCKINNON of Kingston, Ontario, to be a part-time permanent member of the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission, to hold office during good behaviour for a term of four years.

act: Convention for the Conservation of Salmon in the North Atlantic Ocean
precis: Reappointment of CARL McLEAN of North West River, Newfoundland and Labrador, as a Canadian representative to the Council of the North Atlantic Salmon Conservation Organization; to the North American Commission of the North Atlantic Salmon Conservation Organization; and to the West Greenland Commission of the North Atlantic Salmon Conservation Organization, for a term of two years, effective October 18, 2019.

Approval of the appointment by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans of VINCENT CRATE of Koostatak, Manitoba, to be a director of the Board of Directors of the Freshwater Fish Marketing Corporation, to hold office during pleasure for a term of three years, in the place of John Wood, whose term has expired.

Approval of the appointment by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans of THOMAS COLOSIMO of Hay River, Northwest Territories, to be a director of the Board of Directors of the Freshwater Fish Marketing Corporation, to hold office during pleasure for a term of three years, in the place of Bert Buckley, whose term has expired.

Reappointment of PAUL RYALL of Vancouver, British Columbia, as a member of the International Pacific Halibut Commission, to hold office during pleasure for a term of two years, effective November 2, 2019.

act: Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council Act
precis: Appointment of WENDY M. WATSON-WRIGHT of Halifax, Nova Scotia, to be a member of the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council, to hold office during pleasure for a term of one year.

Appointment of ALISON JOANNA KENNEDY of Ottawa, Ontario, to be a full-time member of the Immigration and Refugee Board (Ottawa District Office), to hold office during good behaviour for a term of three years, effective September 16, 2019.

Appointment of MAUREEN LOUISE CARTER-WHITNEY of Toronto, Ontario, to be a part-time member of the Immigration and Refugee Board (Toronto Regional Office), to hold office during good behaviour for a term of three years, effective August 6, 2019.

act: Veterans Review and Appeal Board Act
precis: Appointment of MELANIE MALCHUK of St. Albert, Alberta, to be a permanent member of the Veterans Review and Appeal Board, to hold office during good behaviour for a term of five years, effective August 19, 2019.

Approval of the appointment by the Minister of Canadian Heritage of LUCIO RAGAGNIN of Vaughan, Ontario, to be a member of the Board of Directors of the National Capital Commission, to hold office during pleasure for a term of four years, effective June 22, 2019, in the place of Aditya Jha, whose term has expired.
Re-appointment of CLAUDE JOLI-COEUR of Montréal, Quebec, as Government Film Commissioner, to hold office for a period of three years, effective November 27, 2019.

subject: Regulations Amending the Regulations Establishing a List of Entities
precis: Regulations amending the REGULATIONS ESTABLISHING A LIST OF ENTITIES in order to add FIVE NEW ENTITIES to the list of terrorist entities in respect to support the Government of Canada's efforts to protect Canadians against the threat of terrorism.

subject: Special Economic Measures (Nicaragua) Regulations
precis: SPECIAL ECONOMIC MEASURES (NICARAGUA) REGULATIONS in order to (1) put pressure on the Government of Nicaragua to change its behaviour; (2) communicate a clear message to the Government of Nicaragua that Canada will not accept that gross and systematic human rights violations continue to take place at the hands of the State with impunity; and (3) encourage progress with the negotiation process.

subject: Special Economic Measures (Nicaragua) Permit Authorization Order
precis: Order authorizing the Minister to issue to any individual or person in Canada and any Canadian outside Canada a permit to carry out a specified activity or transaction, or any class of activity or transaction that is otherwise restricted or prohibited pursuant to the Special Economic Measures (Nicaragua) Regulations.

Appointment of the HONOURABLE DEBORAH K. SMITH, Associate Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Nova Scotia, to be Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Nova Scotia, and a Judge ex officio of the Nova Scotia Court of Appeal.
Appointment of the HONOURABLE ANNE L. MACTAVISH, a Judge of the Federal Court, to be a Judge of the Federal Court of Appeal, and a Judge ex officio of the Federal Court.
Appointment of MAHMUD JAMAL, to be a Justice of Appeal of the Court of Appeal for Ontario, and a Judge ex officio of the Superior Court of Justice of Ontario.

Appointment of the HONOURABLE VANESSA V. CHRISTIE, a Judge of the Provincial Court of Ontario, to be a Judge of the Superior Court of Justice of Ontario, and a Judge ex officio of the Court of Appeal for Ontario.
Appointment of the HONOURABLE LUCIE FOURNIER, a puisne Judge of the Superior Court of Quebec for the district of Montréal, to be a puisne Judge of the Court of Appeal of Quebec.
Appointment of the HONOURABLE BENOÎT MOORE, a puisne Judge of the Superior Court of Quebec for the district of Montréal, to be a puisne Judge of the Court of Appeal of Quebec.
Appointment of the HONOURABLE CAROLE A. BEATON, a Judge of the Supreme Court of Nova Scotia, to be Judge of the Nova Scotia Court of Appeal.

Appointment of the HONOURABLE SAMUEL MOREAU, a Judge of the Provincial Court of Nova Scotia, to be a Judge of the Supreme Court of Nova Scotia (Family Division), and a Judge ex officio of the Nova Scotia Court of Appeal.
Appointment of ALAN M. ROSS of the City of Vancouver, in the Province of British Columbia, Barrister-at-law, to be a Judge of the Supreme Court of British Columbia.
Appointment of SHEILA TUCKER of the City of Vancouver, in the Province of British Columbia, one of Her Majesty’s Counsel learned in the law, to be a Judge of the Supreme Court of British Columbia.
Appointment of DAVID A. CRERAR of the City of North Vancouver, in the Province of British Columbia, Barrister-at-law, to be a Judge of the Supreme Court of British Columbia.

Amendment to the Schedule of Order in Council P.C. 2010-1467 of November 25, 2010, as amended by Order in Council P.C. 2011-1714 of December 20, 2011, as amended by Order in Council P.C. 2016-359 of May 18, 2016, by adding the name of the HONOURABLE VICTORIA R. CHIAPPETTA to the roster of superior court judges who may act as members of the Specific Claims Tribunal.
Appointment of the HONOURABLE VICTORIA R. CHIAPPETTA, a Judge of the Superior Court of Justice of Ontario, to be a full-time member of the Specific Claims Tribunal, for a term of five years.

act: Economic Action Plan 2014 Act, No. 1Budget Implementation Act, 2017, No. 1
subject: Order Fixing the Coming into Force of Certain Provisions of (1) the Economic Action Plan 2014 Act, No. 1 on June 1,  2020; and (2) the Budget Implementation Act, 2017, No. 1 on June 1, 2021
precis: Order Fixing (1) June 1, 2020 as the day on which subsection 256(2), sections 257 and 261, subsection 262(3), sections 263 to 266, 293, and 296 of the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (the Act), pursuant to subsection 298(3) of the Economic Action Plan 2014 Act, No. 1, chapter 20 of the Statutes of Canada 2014, COME INTO FORCE; and (2) June 1, 2021 as the day on which subsections 408(1) and 415(2) and (3), section 417, subsections 423(1) and (3) and sections 425 and 438 of this Act, pursuant to subsection 441(1) of the Budget Implementation Act, 2017, No. 1, chapter 20 of the Statutes of Canada, 2017, COME INTO FORCE.

act: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act
subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, 2019
precis: Regulations Amending Certain REGULATIONS MADE UNDER THE PROCEEDS OF CRIME (MONEY LAUNDERING) AND TERRORIST FINANCING ACT, 2019 in order to (1) strengthen Canada’s ability to combat money laundering and terrorist activity financing activities; (2) operationalize changes to the Act and close gaps in Canada’s Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing Regime; (3) help improve reporting entities’ compliance with regulatory requirements; (4) help improve the monitoring and enforcement efforts of Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada; (5) improve Canada’s compliance with international standards; and, (6) adopt minor technical changes.

act: An Act to amend the Customs Act
subject: Order Fixing the Day on which this Order is Made as the Day on which that Act Comes Into Force
precis: Order fixing the day on which this Order is made as the day on which AN ACT TO AMEND THE CUSTOMS ACT, chapter 30 of the Statutes of Canada, 2018, COMES INTO FORCE.

subject: Exit Information Regulations
precis: EXIT INFORMATION REGULATIONS in order to prescribe who must provide exit information, the sources and circumstances of its collection and the specific intervals and manner of its provision to the Canada Border Services Agency.

subject: Regulations Amending the Official Languages (Communications with and Services to the Public) Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the OFFICIAL LANGUAGES (COMMUNICATIONS WITH AND SERVICES TO THE PUBLIC) REGULATIONS in order to better reflect the new realities of Canadian society and to significantly improve them without calling into question their foundations and overall structure.

subject: Regulations Amending the Canada Occupational Health and Safety Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the CANADA OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY REGULATIONS (COHSR) in order to (1) mitigate the risk of injury by updating the references to the standards that are incorporated by reference in PART XII in order to demand compliance with the latest standards that reflect current technical requirements and safety practices required in the work place; (2) modernize the section on fall-protection systems in order to properly reflect industry standards and practices and to reference newly developed standards; (3) eliminate gaps that have caused a reduction in the health and safety protection of employees by bringing the technical requirements up to industry best practices and harmonizing them with other parts of the COHSR, the Code and with other Canadian jurisdictions; and (4) reduce the risk of misinterpretation by clarifying the language in certain sections of Part XII.

subject: Accessible Transportation for Persons with Disabilities Regulations
precis: ACCESSIBLE TRANSPORTATION FOR PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES REGULATIONS in order to promote the inclusion and participation of persons with disabilities in society by creating comprehensive and enforceable accessible transportation requirements that are applicable to all modes of transportation, and enabling persons with disabilities to travel with a predictable and consistent level of accessibility across a barrier-free modern national transportation system.

subject: Regulations Amending the Metal and Diamond Mining Effluent Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the METAL AND DIAMOND MINING EFFLUENT REGULATIONS in order to enable the storage of tailings and waste rock in two water bodies frequented by fish for the Sisson Project.

subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under Part II of the Canada Labour Code (Miscellaneous Program)
precis: Regulations amending CERTAIN REGULATIONS MADE UNDER PART II OF THE CANADA LABOUR CODE (MISCELLANEOUS PROGRAM) in order to (1) correct references to section numbering, typographical or grammatical errors; (2) correct discrepancies between the English and the French versions; (3) add clarity or ensure enforceability of regulatory provisions; (4) improve consistency or harmonize terms with other provisions within or among the regulations; and (5) repeal obsolete or unnecessary regulatory provisions.

subject: Regulations Amending the Income Tax Regulations (2017 Livestock Deferral)
precis: Regulations amending the INCOME TAX REGULATIONS (2017 LIVESTOCK DEFERRAL) in order to implement Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada's advice as to which regions should be prescribed regions on the basis that they have experienced drought or excess moisture conditions.

subject: Regulations Amending the Special Economic Measures (Ukraine) Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the SPECIAL ECONOMIC MEASURES (UKRAINE) REGULATIONS in order to (1) correct the misspelled name of the intended sanctions target, an individual who was involved in Russia's sanctions against Ukrainian vessels and personnel during the November 25, 2018 incident; and (2) align with actions taken by international partners to underscore continued trans-Atlantic unity in responding to Russia's actions in Ukraine.

subject: Order Fixing the Day After the Day on which this Order is Made as the Day on which Section 659 of that Act Comes into Force
precis: Order fixing the day after the day on which this Order is made as the day on which section 659 of the BUDGET IMPLEMENTATION ACT, 2018, NO. 2, chapter 27 of the Statutes of Canada, 2018, COMES INTO FORCE.

subject: International Financial Assistance Regulations
precis: INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE REGULATIONS in order to (1) support the deployment of the International Assistance Innovation Program and the Sovereign Loans Program, as well as the Government's climate repayable contributions programming; (2) establish the parameters for innovative financing within the context of the above-mentioned programs that will address development challenges in developing countries, and support international assistance; and (3) safeguard the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

subject: Regulations Amending the Regulations Implementing the United Nations Resolution on Yemen
precis: Regulations Amending the REGULATIONS IMPLEMENTING THE UNITED NATIONS RESOLUTION ON YEMEN in order to (1) further respond to the ongoing political crisis and conflict in Yemen; (2) fulfill Canada's international legal obligation to implement the binding decisions of the Security Council set out in Resolution 2216 (2015); and (3) address miscellaneous amendments raised by the Standing Joint Committee for the Scrutiny of Regulations.

act: Economic Action Plan 2014 Act, No. 2Economic Action Plan 2015 Act, No. 1
subject: Order Fixing October 30, 2019 as the Day on which Certain Provisions of (1) the Economic Action Plan 2014 Act, No. 2; and (2) the Economic Action Plan 2015 Act, No. 1 Come into Force
precis: Order Fixing October 30, 2019 as the day on which sections (1) 114 to 141 of the ECONOMIC ACTION PLAN 2014 ACT, NO. 2, chapter 39 of the Statutes of Canada, 2014, COME INTO FORCE; and (2) 50 to 53, 56 to 62, 64 and 65 of the ECONOMIC ACTION PLAN 2015 ACT, NO. 1, chapter 36 of the Statutes of Canada, 2015, COME INTO FORCE.

subject: Patent Rules
precis: PATENT RULES in order to (1) implement amendments that were made to the Act in order to allow Canada's ratification of the Patent Law Treaty; and, (2) modernize Canada's patent regime by updating, clarifying, codifying and improving aspects of the regulatory framework.

act: Safeguarding Canada's Seas and Skies Act
subject: Order Fixing the Day on which this Order is Made as the Day on which Certain Provisions of that Act Come into Force
precis: Order fixing the day on which this Order is made as the day on which sections 60 to 62 and 69 and subsections 70(1) to (3) and 71(2) and (4) of the SAFEGUARDING CANADA'S SEAS AND SKIES ACT, chapter 29 of the Statutes of Canada, 2014, COME INTO FORCE.

subject: Environmental Response Regulations
precis: ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE REGULATIONS in order to improve the effectiveness of Canada's Oil Spill Preparedness and Response Regime for prescribed vessels and oil handling facilities while transferring oil to and from vessels.

subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Motor Vehicle Safety Act (Notice of Defect and Notice of Non-compliance)
precis: Regulations Amending CERTAIN REGULATIONS MADE UNDER THE MOTOR VEHICLE SAFETY ACT (NOTICE OF DEFECT AND NOTICE OF NON-COMPLIANCE) in order to (1) improve the alignment of motor vehicle defect and non-compliance requirements with United States requirements; (2) improve motor vehicle safety by making enhanced vehicle safety information available to the Minister, and to vehicle or equipment owners and retailers; and (3) improve departmental oversight of safety defects and instances of non-compliance with the Regulations.

subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Canada Transportation Act (Rail Transport)
precis: Regulations amending certain REGULATIONS MADE UNDER THE CANADA TRANSPORTATION ACT (RAIL TRANSPORT) in order to clarify regulatory requirements and provide the Agency with agile enforcement tools while continuing to provide a sufficient level of regulation to ensure that government policy objectives are met.

subject: Order Amending Schedule 5 to the Canada National Parks Act (Sunshine Village Ski Area)
precis: Order Amending the SCHEDULE 5 to the Canada National Parks Act (Sunshine Village Ski Area) in order to add the name and description of the commercial ski area in the vicinity of Sunshine Village in Banff National Park of Canada, as was intended when the Canada National Parks Act was created in 2000.

subject: Regulations amending the Bank of Canada Notes Regulations
precis: Regulations amending the BANK OF CANADA NOTES REGULATIONS in order allow an additional deputy governor's signature to appear in the place of the Deputy Governor's if that office is vacant.

subject: Order Fixing the Day After the Day on which this Order is Made as the Day on which Subdivisions A and B of Division 7 of Part 6 of that Act Come into Force
precis: Order fixing the day after the day on which the Order is made as the day on which Subdivisions A and B of Division 7 of Part 6 of the BUDGET IMPLEMENTATION ACT, 2018, NO. 1, chapter 12 of the Statutes of Canada, 2018, COME INTO FORCE.

subject: Payment Clearing and Settlement Regulations
precis: PAYMENT CLEARING AND SETTLEMENT REGULATIONS in order to maintain the critical services of a Financial Market Infrastructures, to promote financial stability and to minimize the potential exposure of public funds to loss.

subject: Order Fixing the Day After the Day on which this Order is Made as the Day on which Certain Provisions of that Act Come Into Force
precis: Order fixing the day after the day on which this Order is made as the day on which sections 654, 655 and 658 of the BUDGET IMPLEMENTATION ACT, 2018, NO. 2, chapter 27 of the Statutes of Canada, 2018, COME INTO FORCE.

act: An Act to amend the Canada Business Corporations Act, the Canada Cooperatives Act, the Canada Not-for-profit Corporations Act and the Competition Act
subject: Order Fixing January 1, 2020 as the Day on which Section 24 of that Act Comes into Force
precis: Order fixing January 1, 2020, as the day on which section 24 of AN ACT TO AMEND THE CANADA BUSINESS CORPORATIONS ACT, THE CANADA COOPERATIVES ACT, THE CANADA NOT-FOR-PROFIT CORPORATIONS ACT AND THE COMPETITION ACT, COMES INTO FORCE.

subject: Regulations Amending the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001
precis: Regulations Amending the CANADA BUSINESS CORPORATIONS REGULATIONS, 2001 in order to  to bring into force the diversity disclosure provisions of Bill C-25.

subject: Regulations Amending the Duty Free Shop Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the DUTY FREE SHOP REGULATIONS in order to (1) formally include the modifications announced in the Customs Notice 14-031 in the Regulations; and (2) repeal the Summary of Monthly Sales and the Annual Report requirements.

subject: Regulations Prescribing Physical Injuries
precis: REGULATIONS PRESCRIBING PHYSICAL INJURIES in order to strengthen Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) governance by prescribing a definition of “serious injury” in regulations; in order to clarify when the RCMP must invoke its obligations to initiate an external serious incident investigation as set out in the RCMP Act.

act: National Energy Board ActNational Energy Board Act Part VI (Oil and Gas) Regulations
subject: Issuance of Licence GL-342 - Petrogas Energy Corporation
precis: Order approving the ISSUANCE by the National Energy Board of Licence GL-342 to PETROGAS ENERGY CORPORATION authorizing the exportation of propane, under a new 25-year licence, by Petrogas.

subject: Creation of Reserves - Tsay Keh Dene, British Columbia
precis: Order setting apart 1,241.82 hectares (3,068.60 acres) of lands, for a rural RESERVE CREATION, for the use and benefit of TSAY KEH DENE, FINLAY RIVER INDIAN RESERVE NO. 6, MESILINKA INDIAN RESERVE NO. 7 AND INGENIKA INDIAN RESERVE NO. 8, in British Columbia.

subject: Gambler First Nation Indian Reserve 63B, in Manitoba
precis: Order setting apart 3.062 hectares (7.57 acres), including mines and minerals, for the use and benefit of the Gambler First Nation, as a new reserve to be known as GAMBLER FIRST NATION INDIAN RESERVE 63B, in Manitoba.

subject: Reserve Creation - Metepenagiag Mi'kmaq Nation - Metepenagiag Urban reserve 8, New Brunswick
precis: Order setting apart 3.58 hectares (8.85 acres) of land, excluding mines and minerals, for the use and benefit of the Metepenagiag Mi'kmaq Nation, as a new reserve to be known as METEPENAGIAG URBAN RESERVE 8, in New Brunswick.

subject: Pheasant Rump Nakota Indian Reserve No. 68, Saskatchewan ** Grant of Easement **
precis: Order consenting to the exercise by SASKATCHEWAN POWER CORPORATION of the power to take an interest in lands in an Indian reserve without the consent of the owner, and to authorize, in lieu of such taking, the grant of the required easement.

subject: Relinquishement of the administration and control from the Commissioner of Northwest Territories
precis: Order consenting to the RELINQUISHMENT in perpetuity, by the Commissioner of Northwest Territories, of the administration and control of the surface rights of the lands at the Cantung Exclusion Area in the Northwest Territories that were originally transferred to the Commissioner of Northwest Territories under the Northwest Territories Lands and Resources Devolution Transfer Agreement on April 1, 2014.

subject: Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in Self-Government Agreement
precis: Order authorizing the amendments to Schedule A and Part 3 of Schedule B of the TR'ONDËK HWËCH'IN SELF-GOVERNMENT AGREEMENT.

subject: European Space Agency
precis: Order authorizing the Minister of Industry and designated officials of the Canadian Space Agency to commit the Government of Canada to EUROPEAN SPACE AGENCY optional programs.

subject: Order Authorizing to sign, execute and issue an Instrument of Full Powers, subject to ratification, the Audiovisual Coproduction Treaty between the Government of Canada and the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine
precis: Order Authorizing (a) the Minister of Foreign Affairs to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the AUDIOVISUAL COPRODUCTION TREATY BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT OF CANADA AND THE CABINET OF MINISTERS OF UKRAINE; or (b) the Minister of Foreign Affairs to execute and issue an Instrument of Full Powers authorizing the individuals mentioned in the order, to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the AUDIOVISUAL COPRODUCTION TREATY BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT OF CANADA AND THE CABINET OF MINISTERS OF UKRAINE.

subject: Order Authorizing to sign, execute and issue and Instrument of Full Powers, subject to ratification, the Exchange of Notes between the Government of Canada and the Government of the United States of America
precis: Order Authorizing (a) the Minister of Foreign Affairs to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the EXCHANGE OF NOTES BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT OF CANADA AND THE GOVERNMENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA CONSTITUTING AN AGREEMENT AMENDING CHAPTER 4 OF ANNEX IV OF THE TREATY BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT OF CANADA AND THE GOVERNMENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA CONCERNING PACIFIC SALMON DONE AT OTTAWA ON JANUARY 28, 1985, AS AMENDED (Agreement); or (b) the Minister of Foreign Affairs to execute and issue an Instrument of Full Powers authorizing the individuals mentioned in the order, to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the Agreement.

subject: Patent Law Treaty
precis: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary to ratify, on behalf of Canada, the PATENT LAW TREATY, done at Geneva on June 1, 2000.

act: Federal Public Sector Labour Relations Act
subject: Canadian Food Inspection Agency - Professional Institute of the Public Service of Canada ** Collective Agreement **
precis: Order approving the ENTRY by the Canadian Food Inspection Agency into a COLLECTIVE AGREEMENT with the PROFESSIONAL INSTITUTE OF THE PUBLIC SERVICE OF CANADA applicable to all employees of the Agency in the Scientific and Analytical  Bargaining Unit, which provides for the changes to the previous Collective Agreement and which expires on September 30, 2018.

subject: Wahta Mohawk Land Claim Settlement Agreement
precis: Order confirming Article 3 of the WAHTA MOHAWK LAND CLAIM SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT (the Settlement Agreement), dated December 1, 2002, among the Wahta Mohawks (First Nation), Her Majesty the Queen in right of Ontario (Ontario) and Her Majesty the Queen in right of Canada (Canada) as a Specific Agreement.

subject: Mohawk of the Bay of Quinte First Nation Agreement
precis: Order confirming the FINAL AGREEMENT, dated November 3, 2004, among the MOHAWKS OF THE BAY OF QUINTE FIRST NATION (First Nation), Her Majesty the Queen in right of Ontario (Ontario) and Her Majesty the Queen in right of Canada (Canada) as a Specific Agreement.

subject: Mitaanjigamiing Treaty Land Entitlement Claim Settlement Agreement
precis: Order in Council confirming Article 5 of the MITAANJIGAMIING TREATY LAND ENTITLEMENT CLAIM SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT dated July 24, 2017, among the First Nation, Ontario and Canada as a Specific Agreement.

subject: Biinjitiwaabik Zaaging Anishinaabek First Nation ** Agreement **
precis: Order Confirming the FINAL AGREEMENT, dated October 3, 2016, among the BIINJITIWAABIK ZAAGING ANISHINAABEK FIRST NATION, Her Majesty the Queen in Right of Canada and Her Majesty the Queen in Right of Ontario, as a SPECIFIC AGREEMENT.

subject: Chapleau Cree First Nation, Ontario ** Confirmation **
precis: Order requesting to confirm Article 7 of the Chapleau Cree Treaty Land Entitlement Claim Settlement Agreement, dated November 27, 2015, among Chapleau Cree First Nation, Her Majesty the Queen in right of Ontario and Her Majesty the Queen in right of Canada as a SPECIFIC AGREEMENT.

subject: Provincial Emergency Financial Assistance Order No. 220, New Brunswick
precis: PROVINCIAL EMERGENCY FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE ORDER NO. 220 which makes a declaration of federal concern and authorizes the Minister to provide financial assistance to the province of NEW BRUNSWICK, with respect to the heavy rainfall that occurred from January 23 to 24, 2019.

subject: Fort Erie Jaycees - Ontario ** Dissolution **
precis: Order approving the DISSOLUTION OF THE FORT ERIE JAYCEES, in Ontario.

subject: Chambre de commerce au Coeur de la Montérégie - Quebec ** Change of Boundaries **
precis: Order approving the application by the CHAMBRE DE COMMERCE AU COEUR DE LA MONTÉRÉGIE, in Quebec, to CHANGE THE BOUNDARIES of its district from the Marieville, Sainte-Angèle-de-Monnoir, Rougemont and St-Césaire to Marieville, Rougemont, Saint-Césaire, Sainte-Angèle-de-Monnoir, Saint-Paul d'Abbotsford and Ange-Gardien.

subject: Large Diameter Line Pipe Anti-dumping Duty Remission Order
precis: LARGE DIAMETER LINE PIPE ANTI-DUMPING DUTY REMISSION ORDER in order to provide a remedy in response to the short supply of large diameter line pipe in the Canadian market for certain specific projects.

subject: Order Amending the United States Surtax Remission Order, No. 2019-2
precis: ORDER AMENDING THE UNITED STATES SURTAX REMISSION ORDER, NO. 2019-2 in order to (1) provide retroactive relief from surtaxes on additional steel, aluminum and other goods, determined to be in short supply in Canada at the time of importation; (2) provide retroactive relief from surtaxes for additional specific companies that cannot avoid the surtaxes due to existing contractual obligations or particular exceptional circumstances to source steel and aluminum from the United States; and (3) make technical amendments to ensure that the scope of remission of surtaxes for steel and aluminum products already covered under the Order applies as intended.

subject: Regulations Amending the Special Economic Measures (Venezuela) Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the SPECIAL ECONOMIC MEASURES (VENEZUELA) REGULATIONS in order to (1) demonstrate that Canada's sanctions are not intended to be permanent; (2) send a clear message to members of the Maduro regime that Canada is willing to review the list of Venezuelan officials sanctioned as long as they support the return to democracy in Venezuela; and (3) show solidarity with the actions of the United States.

subject: Regulations Amending the Excise Duties on Cannabis Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the EXCISE DUTIES ON CANNABIS REGULATIONS in order to change the rates of additional excise duty in respect of the coordinated province and territories that apply in respect of cannabis products that are edible cannabis, cannabis extracts and cannabis topicals.

subject: Regulations Amending the Fuel Charge Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the FUEL CHARGE REGULATIONS in order to (1) provide fuel charge relief on natural gas and light fuel oil for remote power plant operators that generate electricity for remote communities; (2) provide partial fuel charge relief on natural gas and propane used in eligible greenhouse activities; (3) provide a rebate of the fuel charge to registered distributors for fuel that is delivered to, and subsequently exported from Canada by, non-registered, non-resident persons, subject to certain conditions; (4) facilitate the integration with the federal fuel charge of facilities that are covered by the provincial output-based performance standards system in Saskatchewan; (5) expand relief of the fuel charge for farmers, such that a registered distributor can deliver, without the fuel charge applying, gasoline and light fuel oil to a farmer at a cardlock facility, subject to certain conditions; and (6) incorporate technical amendments to ensure the proper functioning of the fuel charge system.

subject: Remission Order of Federal Administrative Fees Paid or Payable by the Yukon and the Northwest Territories
precis: REMISSION ORDER in respect of federal administrative fees paid or to be paid by Yukon and the Northwest Territories (NWT) for set-up costs related to the rebate programs put in place by the territories to return the proceeds of carbon pollution pricing to their residents and businesses.

subject: Agreement with Prince Edward Island - Agricultural Disaster Relief Program
precis: Order authorizing the Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food to ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND to provide federal contributions of up to $9,360,000 under the Agricultural Disaster Relief Program to assist affected agricultural producers with the extraordinary costs related to the excess moisture and cold temperatures experienced during the 2018 harvest.

subject: National Aboriginal Economic Development Appointment Process and Name Change

Order directing that a WARRANT be prepared authorizing the expenditure of sums set forth in APPROPRIATION ACT NO. 1, 2020-21.
[RELEASE OF THE MAIN ESTIMATES INTERIM SUPPLY FOR 2020-21]

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 Coronavirus Disease in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 CORONAVIRUS DISEASE IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA) in order to protect the health and safety of the public from the COVID-19 coronavirus disease outbreak by banning entry of certain foreign nationals travelling to Canada by air from all countries with the exception of persons travelling from the United States.

subject: Order Fixing the Day on Which this Order is Registered as the Day on Which Certain Sections of that Act Come into Force
precis: Order fixing the day on which this Order is registered as the day on which sections 236, 241, 249, 252 to 254, 256 and 267 of the BUDGET IMPLEMENTATION ACT, 2019, NO. 1, chapter 29 of the Statutes of Canada, 2019, COME INTO FORCE.

subject: Regulations Maintaining the Safety of Persons in Ports and the Seaway
precis: Regulations maintaining the SAFETY OF PERSONS IN PORTS AND THE SEAWAY in order to minimize the risk of COVID-19 spreading to port and Seaway workers who directly interact with cruise ship crew and passengers during regular operations.

subject: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations
precis: Regulations amending the IMMIGRATION AND REFUGEE PROTECTION REGULATIONS in order to help support the Government's response to COVID-19 pandemic to implement any decision to restrict entry into Canada and to ensure the ongoing integrity of our borders in the economic interests of Canada and the health and safety of Canadians.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to protect the health of the public from the introduction or spread of the COVID-19 coronavirus disease transmitted via travellers from foreign countries by prohibiting entry into Canada by foreign nationals for optional or discretionary purposes.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other Than the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to enhance recent border measures to minimize the risk of exposure to COVID-19 coronavirus disease from being transmitted by travellers entering Canada from foreign countries.

subject: Regulations Amending the Atlantic Pilotage Tariff Regulations, 1996
precis: Regulations amending the ATLANTIC PILOTAGE TARIFF REGULATIONS, 1996 in order to enable the Authority to meet its mandate to operate a safe and efficient pilotage service within the Atlantic region, while achieving financial self-sufficiency of individual ports (i.e. avoiding cross-subsidization).

subject: Regulations Amending the Pacific Pilotage Tariff Regulations
precis: Regulations amending the PACIFIC PILOTAGE TARIFF REGULATIONS in order to (1) maintain tariffs that are fair and reasonable that permit the Authority to operate on a financially self-sustaining basis, while continuing to deliver pilotage related services that are safe, efficient and reliable; (2) ensure adequate revenue to pay for a new pilot launch as part of the Authority’s launch replacement program; and (3) clarify in the Regulations when a delay charge applies so that the wording aligns with the Authority’s intent, as well as with the industry’s current practices.

subject: Regulations Amending the Great Lakes Pilotage Tariff Regulations
precis: Regulations amending the GREAT LAKES PILOTAGE TARIFF REGULATIONS in order to (1) levy tariffs that are fair and reasonable to remain financially self-sufficient; (2) continue to recruit and train apprentice pilots; (3) fulfill obligations associated with the purchase of a pilot boat as per the terms of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the United States Coast Guard; (4) introduce a cost-recovery mechanism to recover incremental pilot compensation when pilots remain on vessels on overtime beyond their original assignment to reduce delays to vessels due to a shortage of pilots; (5) standardize the docking/undocking and stoppage charges in all districts as to generate sufficient charges to re-main financially self-sufficient; (6) continue to enlist services from the service provider between the St. Lambert and the Beauharnois Locks; (7) formalize the recovery of pilot travel costs in the Regulations; (8) ensure greater clarity in provisions identified by the SJCSR; and (9) generate revenues to cover the new Pilotage Act administration charge, as set out in the new section 37.1 of the Act.

subject: Order Declaring that the Provisions of the Regulations Respecting Reduction in the Release of Methane and Certain Volatile Organic Compounds (Upstream Oil and Gas Sector) Do Not Apply in British Columbia
precis: ORDER DECLARING THAT THE PROVISIONS OF THE REGULATIONS RESPECTING REDUCTION IN THE RELEASE OF METHANE AND CERTAIN VOLATILE ORGANIC COMPOUNDS (UPSTREAM OIL AND GAS SECTOR) DO NOT APPLY IN BRITISH COLUMBIA in order to reduce regulatory overlap and reporting burden, while allowing British Columbia to achieve equivalent methane emission reductions in the oil and gas sector in a manner that best suits its particular circumstances.

subject: Arrangement between the Government of Canada and the European Space Agency concerning the Participation in the advance Research in Telecommunications Systems 4.0 (ARTES 4.0)
precis: Order Authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to sign and to bring into force, or to delegate the authority to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, the ARRANGEMENT BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT OF CANADA AND THE EUROPEAN SPACE AGENCY CONCERNING THE PARTICIPATION BY THE GOVERNMENT OF CANADA IN THE ADVANCE RESEARCH IN TELECOMMUNICATIONS SYSTEMS 4.0 (ARTES 4.0) PROGRAMME.

subject: Lease with BBC Golf Ltd. ** NCC **

subject: United States Enforcement Officers Exemption Order, 2020 - Marine Transportation of Firearms

subject: Aggregate borrowing limit
precis: Order (1) authorizing the Minister of Finance to borrow money on behalf of the Government of Canada and conducting activities related to the borrowing of money as he considers appropriate; (2) specifying $350 billion as the aggregate principal amount of money that the Minister of Finance may borrow in the period beginning on April 1, 2020 and ending on March 31, 2021; (3) designating which officials within the Department of Finance Canada and the Bank of Canada can sign and countersign security certificates; (4) authorizing the Minister of Finance to appoint fiscal agents and registrars; (5) authorizing payments out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the management of the public debt.

subject: Regulations Amending the Canada Grain Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the CANADA GRAIN REGULATIONS in order to (1) update the Canada Grain Regulations to align with the amendments to the Canada Grain Act contained in the Act to implement Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement; (2) ensure that the CGC can continue to meet its mandate ‘to ensure a dependable commodity for domestic and export markets’; and (3) improve consistency of language between English and French text.

subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Customs Tariff (Miscellaneous Program)
precis: Regulations amending CERTAIN MADE UNDER THE CUSTOMS TARIFF (MISCELLANEOUS PROGRAM) in order to support the seamless transition from the North American Free Trade Agreement to Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) and to ensure stakeholders will have current and clear regulations in place at the time of implementation of CUSMA.

subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Special Import Measures Act (Miscellaneous Program)
precis: Regulations amending CERTAIN REGULATIONS MADE UNDER THE SPECIAL IMPORT MEASURES ACT (MISCELLANEOUS PROGRAM) in order to implement the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement outcome concerning trade remedies.

subject: Regulations Amending the Canadian International Trade Tribunal Procurement Inquiry Regulations (Miscellaneous Program)
precis: Regulations amending the CANADIAN INTERNATIONAL TRADE TRIBUNAL PROCUREMENT INQUIRY REGULATIONS (MISCELLANEOUS PROGRAM) in order to support Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA)  implementation by implementing the CUSMA outcomes concerning government procurement and bilateral safeguards.

subject: Regulations Amending the Canadian International Trade Tribunal Regulations (Miscellaneous Program)
precis: Regulations amending the CANADIAN INTERNATIONAL TRADE TRIBUNAL REGULATIONS (MISCELLANEOUS PROGRAM) in order to support Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA)  implementation by implementing the CUSMA outcomes concerning government procurement and bilateral safeguards.

subject: Order Amending the Courier Imports Remission Order
precis: Order amending the COURIER IMPORTS REMISSION ORDER in order to implement Canada's negotiated commitments in the Canada-United-States-Mexico in respect of DE MINIMIS thresholds.

act: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions Act

subject: Order Amending the Import Control List

subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Export and Import Permits Act

subject: Export Charges for Certain Dairy Products Regulations
precis: EXPORT CHARGES FOR CERTAIN DAIRY PRODUCTS REGULATIONS in order to ensure that Canada complies with its international commitments and supports the implementation of Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement.

subject: Regulations Amending the Food and Drug Regulations (Finished Product Testing)

subject: Regulations Amending the Food and Drug Regulations (Distribution of Drugs as Samples)
precis: Regulations Amending the FOOD AND DRUG REGULATIONS (DISTRIBUTION OF DRUGS AS SAMPLES) in order to (1) fully implement Canada’s Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) commitment to permit the distribution of certain low risk Non-prescription drugs (NPDs) and natural health products (NHPs) as samples, under certain conditions; (2) allow Health Canada to consider other NPDs for distribution as samples to the general public after further analysis and to respond to health and safety risks; (3) update the list of practitioners to whom samples of drugs may be distributed, in order to align federal law with the various practitioners’ scope of practice under provincial and territorial law; and (4) replace a reference to Article 1711 of North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) in the Food and Drug Regulations (FDR) with a reference to Articles 20.48 and 20.49 of the CUSMA.

subject: Regulations Amending the Natural Health Products Regulations (Distribution of Natural Health Products as Samples)
precis: Regulations Amending the NATURAL HEALTH PRODUCTS REGULATIONS (DISTRIBUTION OF NATURAL HEALTH PRODUCTS AS SAMPLES) in order to (1) fully implement Canada’s Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) commitment to permit the distribution of certain low risk Non-prescription drugs (NPDs) and natural health products (NHPs) as samples, under certain conditions; (2) allow Health Canada to consider other NPDs for distribution as samples to the general public after further analysis and to respond to health and safety risks; (3) update the list of practitioners to whom samples of drugs may be distributed, in order to align federal law with the various practitioners’ scope of practice under provincial and territorial law; and (4) replace a reference to Article 1711 of North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) in the Food and Drug Regulations (FDR) with a reference to Articles 20.48 and 20.49 of the CUSMA.

subject: Regulations Amending the Investment Canada Regulations (Miscellaneous Program)
precis: Regulations amending the INVESTMENT CANADA REGULATIONS (MISCELLANEOUS PROGRAM) in order to (1) support the implementation of the Canada–United States–Mexico Agreement; and (2) ensure the regulations continue to be effective.

subject: Direction to the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission Respecting the Implementation of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement
precis: DIRECTION TO THE CANADIAN RADIO-TELEVISION AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS COMMISSION RESPECTING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE CANADA–UNITED STATES–MEXICO AGREEMENT in order to (1) implement the Canada–United States–Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) commitments to implement paragraphs 1 and 4 of Annex 15-D of CUSMA; and (2) allow the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) to follow its own established rule-making process to give effect to the commitments and preserves the CRTC's independence.
