subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) allow the entry of extended family members of a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident; (4) allow entry on compassionate grounds; (5) allow the entry of students to attend a listed institution, effective October 20, 2020; and (6) make non-substantive administrative amendments for clarity.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country other than the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to restrict entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from countries other than the United States, with some limited exemptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) allow the entry of extended family members of a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident; (4) allow entry on compassionate grounds; (5) allow the entry of students to attend a listed institution, effective October 20, 2020; and (6) make non-substantive administrative amendments for clarity.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions; even those who are exempted from the prohibition may not enter if they have COVID-19, or they exhibit signs and symptoms of COVID-19; (3) allow immediate family members and extended family members of a person registered as an Indian under the Indian Act to enter Canada; (4) clarify that entry will be denied to foreign nationals if they seek to enter a province or territory for purposes of compassionate grounds without quarantining for 14 days, and that province or territory has provided written notice of objection to such releases from quarantine to the Minister of Health; entry will also be denied if the person in charge of any location a foreign national intends to visit for compassionate reasons during the 14-day quarantine period objects to this.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from countries other than the United States, unless they meet a specified list of exemptions; even those who are exempted from the general prohibition may not enter if they have COVID-19, or they exhibit signs and symptoms of COVID-19; (3) allow immediate family members and extended family members of a person registered as an Indian under the Indian Act, to enter Canada; (4) continue to allow foreign nationals to enter Canada for certain compassionate reasons; (5) clarify that entry will be denied to foreign nationals if they seek to enter a province or territory for purposes of compassionate grounds without quarantining for 14 days, and that province or territory has provided, through their public health officials, written notice of objection to such releases from quarantine to the Minister of Health; entry will also be denied if the person in charge of any location a foreign national intends to visit for compassionate reasons during the 14 -day quarantine period objects to this.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Mandatory Isolation), No. 7
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (MANDATORY ISOLATION), NO. 7  in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who enter Canada, whether by air, land, rail and sea, are required to answer questions to determine if they have signs or symptoms of COVID-19, and, with limited exceptions, quarantine or isolate for 14 days from the day upon which they entered Canada; (3) continue to require persons entering Canada to provide information requested; (4) introduce authorities to mandate pre-border and post-border information reporting for travelers; (5) specify further conditions on the compassionate grounds exemption; (6) add exemptions relating to students who regularly cross the Canada-U.S. border for school, dependent children subject to cross-border custody arrangements, residents of certain isolated cross-border communities and persons denied entry to the U.S. at a land border and immediately turned back; and (7) enable joint federal-provincial pilot projects for an alternative approach to the current 14-day quarantine requirement.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from countries other than the United States, with some limited exemptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) clarify that dating partners must be over the age of 18 to qualify for the extended family exception; (4) allow entry of foreign national athletes and support personnel participating or engaging in certain high-performance international single sport events; and (5) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until January 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Mandatory Isolation), No. 8
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (MANDATORY ISOLATION), NO. 8  in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) exempt athletes and support personnel participating in or engaging in certain high-performance international single sport events from the requirement to quarantine under specified conditions; (4) remove clauses that are expired, and update clause references accordingly; and (5) make minor edits for improved readability.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country;  (2)  continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) clarify the definition of extended family member in an exclusive dating relationship to specify that both persons in the relationship must be 18 years of age or older; (4) exempt foreign national athletes and support personnel participating in or engaging in certain high-performance international single sport events from the prohibition on entry; (5) clarify that any foreign national enrolled in a learning program at a listed institution need to hold or may hold a valid study permit; and (6) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until December 21, 2020.

precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) specify that persons exempt under the Aeronautics Act from the pre-flight testing are now required to test upon their return to Canada, with limited exemptions for certain classes of persons listed in the Order, or in extraordinary circumstances as determined by the Quarantine Officer at entry; (4) provide the option to present proof of a positive COVID-19 result of a test performed 14 - 90 days prior to the initial scheduled departure time, instead of a negative COVID-19 test; and (5) clarify that Canadian cross-border students studying in the U.S. are prohibited from providing direct care for persons over 65 years of age within the first 14 days after their entry into Canada, and that all passengers travelling in a vehicle at a land border crossing who were denied entry into the U.S. will be required to quarantine if any of the travelers exited the vehicle abroad.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) require all travellers, with limited exceptions, entering from the U.S. by land to also provide evidence of a negative COVID-19 molecular test done in the U.S. not more than 72 hours prior to presenting at the port of entry, or present proof of a positive COVID-19 result of a test performed 14 - 90 days prior to the initial scheduled arrival time; (4) require all travellers to undergo a COVID-19 molecular test at the time of entry and once again during the 14 day entry period while in quarantine; (5) require all travellers to provide their contact information and a suitable quarantine plan electronically prior to seeking entry to Canada; (6) require travellers entering by air to enter a government-authorized accommodation near the first port of entry while awaiting the first post-entry test, and require them to submit evidence that they have pre-booked and pre-paid for accommodation for a three-day period prior to boarding their flight to Canada, which will be verified on arrival; (7) include more stringent requirements for a suitable quarantine plan to strengthen the mandatory 14-day quarantine, and further clarify that travellers in quarantine or isolation are required to answer questions and provide information to peace officers on request; (8) add exceptions for persons providing essential services, persons seeking essential medical treatment outside of Canada, persons entering Canada to assist in a major disaster, and unaccompanied dependent children; (9) expand on the obligations of quarantine-exempt travellers with respect to mask wearing and maintaining a list of contacts during their initial 14 day period in Canada; and (10) extend the effect of the Order to April 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) prohibit foreign nationals from entering Canada from the U.S. if they fail to meet the pre-arrival testing obligations; and (4) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until March 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) prohibit foreign nationals from entering Canada from the U.S. if they fail to meet the pre-arrival testing obligations; and (4) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until April 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) continue to require all travellers, with limited exceptions, entering from the U.S. by land to also provide evidence of a negative COVID-19 molecular test done in the U.S. not more than 72 hours prior to presenting at the port of entry, or present proof of a positive COVID-19 result of a test performed 14 - 90 days prior to the initial scheduled arrival time; (4) continue to require all travellers to undergo a COVID-19 molecular test at the time of entry and once again during the 14 day entry period while in quarantine; (5) continue to require all travellers to provide their contact information and a suitable quarantine plan electronically prior to seeking entry to Canada; (6) continue to require travellers entering by air to enter a government-authorized accommodation near the first port of entry while awaiting the first post-entry test, and require them to submit evidence that they have pre-booked and pre-paid for accommodation for a three-day period prior to boarding their flight to Canada, which will be verified on arrival; (7) prohibit entrants to travel to their government authorized accommodation VIA means of public transportation; and (8) extend the effect of the Order to April 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (4) extend the effect of the Order to May 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) amend the extended family member exception to provide that the required statutory declaration should be provided by the parent of a minor rather than by the minor (if applicable); (4) add a national interest exemption to align with the one that exists in the non-US entry Order; (5) make non-substantive administrative changes for clarity and to better align the English and French versions; (6) continue to maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (7) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until June 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from countries other than the United States, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) amend the extended family member exception to provide that the required statutory declaration should be provided by the parent of a minor rather than by the minor (if applicable); (4) amend the extended family member exception to provide that a statutory declaration is not required where the relationship has been verified through the permanent residence application and approval process; (5) make non-substantive administrative changes for clarity and to better align the English and French versions; (6) continue to maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (7) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until June 21, 2021;

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) authorize the Chief Public Health Officer to take immediate public health measures by imposing conditions or requirements on persons who are otherwise excepted from requirements set out in the Order; (4) clarify a number of existing requirements and exceptions; (5) maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (6) extend the effect of the Order to June 21, 2021.

precis: Rules Amending the FEDERAL COURTS IMMIGRATION AND REFUGEE PROTECTION RULES in order to (1) require that a party identify the name of the person who prepares, for a fee or other consideration, the application for leave and judicial review; (2) introduce a new provision that consolidates a number of separate provisions regarding the deemed receipt of documents that are "sent," including the option for electronic transmission, and aims to align these Rules with the modernized Federal Courts Rules regarding the deemed receipt of documents that are "served"; (3) introduce a simplified procedure to request an anonymity order; (4) introduce a requirement for the applicant to file a statement indicating the language of the hearing and of the materials in the court record; and (5) amend the definition of an "appeal" to reflect the changes under the Citizenship Act.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) continue to maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (4) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until July 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from countries other than the United States, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) allow any person approved as a permanent resident under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act to enter Canada; (4) continue to maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (5) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until July 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) provide an exception from the quarantine requirement for fully vaccinated persons, and require mandatory traveller declarations on vaccination status and proof of vaccination as of July 5, 2021; (4) clarify a number of existing requirements and exceptions; (5) maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (6) extend the effect of the Order to July 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) continue to maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (4) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until August 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from countries other than the United States, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) continue to maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (4) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until August 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (4) extend the effect of the Order to August 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the United States for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) permit fully vaccinated citizens and permanent residents of the United States and their unvaccinated dependants to enter Canada for discretionary travel effective August 9, 2021; (4) exempt fully vaccinated immediate and extended family members of a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person registered as an Indian under the Indian Act, from demonstrating their intent to stay in Canada for a period of at least 15 days effective August 9, 2021; (5) allow unvaccinated habitual residents of the remote communities of Point Roberts, Washington; Northwest Angle, Minnesota; and Hyder, Alaska to enter a neighbouring Canadian community for optional or discretionary purposes effective August 9, 2021; (6) allow persons to enter Canadian waters, provided that they remain on board their vessel and do not make contact with another conveyance, anchor, or moor while in Canadian waters effective August 9, 2021; (7) allow persons to leave Canadian waters and return to Canada, provided that they remain on board their vessel and do not make contact with another conveyance, anchor, or moor while outside of Canada effective August 9, 2021; (8) permit fully vaccinated foreign nationals from any country to enter Canada from the United States for discretionary travel as of September 7, 2021; and (9) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until September 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from countries other than the United States, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) allow fully vaccinated French citizens residing in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon to enter Canada for discretionary travel effective August 9, 2021; (4) allow persons to enter Canada in marine mode, provided that they remain on board their vessel and do not make contact with another conveyance, anchor, or moor while in Canadian waters, effective August 9, 2021; (5) allow persons to leave Canadian waters and return to Canada, provided that they remain on board their vessel and do not make contact with another conveyance, anchor, or moor while outside of Canada, effective August 9, 2021; (6) exempt fully vaccinated immediate and extended family members of a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person registered as an Indian under the Indian Act, from demonstrating their intent to stay in Canada for a period of at least 15 days, effective August 9, 2021; (7) permit fully vaccinated foreign nationals from any country and their unvaccinated dependants to enter Canada for discretionary travel as of September 7, 2021; and (8) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until September 21, 2021.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain all requirements for all unvaccinated travellers to have a COVID-19 molecular test result before entering Canada, to undergo testing when entering and once again later in the 14-day post entry period, and to quarantine upon entry to Canada, subject to limited exceptions; (3) maintain mandatory traveller declarations on vaccination status, proof of vaccination, public health measures, and testing requirements for fully vaccinated persons; (4) exempt fully vaccinated persons entering by air or land from the requirement to quarantine provided they fulfill certain conditions; (5) remove the requirement for incoming air travellers to remain in government-authorized accommodations while they wait for the result of their on arrival test; (6) reduce the isolation period for symptomatic persons (and those testing positive) from 14 days to 10 days, based on th latest evidence on the infectious period of COVID-19; (7) require full vaccinated foreign nationals seeking to enter Canada for a discretionary purpose by air mode to submit proof of vaccination prior to boarding a flight to Canada; (8) exempt unvaccinated children under the age of 12 who enter Canada with a fully vaccinated parent or guardian from quarantine, subject to enhanced public health measures; (9) exempt from quarantine persons over the age of 12 who are medically unable to receive a vaccine, subject to enhanced public health measures; (10) exempt from quarantine unvaccinated habitual residents of the remote communities of Point Roberts, Washington; Northwest Angle, Minnesota; and Hyder, Alaska when entering neighbouring Canadian communities to carry out everyday functions; (11) allow persons with a right of entry returning to Canada by land following travel to the United States, for less than 72 hours, to complete their pre-arrival test in Canada rather than in the United States; (12) provide the Chief Pubic Health Officer with the authority to implement, as needed, a surveillance-based testing program through mandatory randomized testing; (13) require persons travelling to Canada by marine vessel to have a negative COVID-19 test result before entering Canada, with limited exceptions; (14) restrict limited release from quarantine provisions on compassionate grounds to urgent situations that preclude the ability to plan for quarantine; (15) allow fully vaccinated travellers to provide direct care for persons 65 years and older during the 14 days following entry, while maintaining the prohibition for unvaccinated persons; (16) refine requirements for suitable isolation plans to include shared bathroom criteria; (17) increase the entry time limit for those who test positive as a result of a prior infection (from 14 to 180 days before entry, rather than from 14 to 90 days before entry); (18) require essential service travellers with a Chief Public Health Officer exemption from quarantine to submit vaccination status information, effective September 7, 2021; and (19) extend the effect of the Order until September 21, 2021.

precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry of foreign nationals arriving from the United States, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) replace the prohibition of entry from optional or discretionary to prohibition of entry if not fully vaccinated, with certain exceptions; (4) remove the prohibition of entry for asylum claimants entering between ports of entry; and (5) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until January 31, 2022.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) provide the Chief Public Health Officer with flexibility to adjust pre-arrival testing measures based on scientific evidence; (3) enables the Minister of Health, on the recommendation of the Chief Public Health Officer, to designate classes of persons who have a contraindication that prevents their being vaccinated against COVID-19 due to a medical reason; (4) remove the requirement for fully vaccinated Canadian citizens, permanent residents of Canada, and persons registered under the Indian Act to provide proof of a negative COVID-19 molecular test taken within 72 hours prior to boarding a flight or upon arrival at a land border, when travelling outside of Canada for less than 72 hours; (5) remove or amend certain pre-arrival testing, post-arrival testing and quarantine exemptions, in alignment with the removal or amendment of these categories of permitted entrant from the orders restricting entry to Canada; and (6) extend the duration of the measures until January 31, 2022.

precis:

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry of foreign nationals, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) grant authority to the Minister of Health to temporarily prohibit entry of foreign nationals, irrespective of vaccination status, if in the 14 days prior to entering Canada they were in a country identified as having an outbreak of a variant of concern as identified by the World Health Organization; (4) clarify some of the entry requirements for foreign nationals based on vaccination status; and (5) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until February 28, 2022.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) allow for selective verification of pre-arrival COVID-19 tests by border services officers for travellers entering Canada at land or marine points of entry; (3) clarify that unvaccinated operators of a commercial vehicle, unless delivering medically necessary supplies, equipment, or devices, are not exempt from the requirement to obtain a pre-arrival COVID-19 test and will be subject to the requirement to quarantine and to undergo COVID-19 molecular testing in Canada; (4) provide residents of Saint Pierre and Miquelon an exemption from quarantine and on-arrival testing, regardless of vaccination status, when scheduled to receive medical care within 96 hours of arrival; and (5) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until February 28, 2022.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry of foreign nationals, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) permit entry of unvaccinated children and dependent persons entering Canada with a parent or guardian with a medical contraindication to vaccination; (4) include entry via British Columbia in the pre-existing exemption for habitual residents of Alaska who enter Canada via Yukon to access another place in Alaska or to return to their place of residence; and (5) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until March 31, 2022.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry of foreign nationals, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) permit unvaccinated, symptomatic or COVID-19 positive foreign national cruise ship passengers to enter Canada if they remain in isolation on board the vessel for the duration of their stay in Canada; (4) permit symptomatic or COVID-19 positive foreign national cruise ship passengers who would otherwise be permitted entry to Canada to disembark at their final destination in Canada to complete their isolation on land; (5) allow foreign nationals to enter without a valid COVID-19 pre-arrival test if they are exempt from the pre-arrival testing requirements set out in the Quarantine Order; and (6) clarify existing entry exemptions for certain foreign nationals to include those entering to be accredited by Global Affairs Canada.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) exempt fully vaccinated travellers from pre-arrival COVID-19 testing as of April 1, 2022; (3) exempt unvaccinated children who are under 12 accompanied by a fully vaccinated parent/guardian from pre-arrival COVID-19 testing, as of April 25, 2022; (4) subject unvaccinated children aged between 5 and 12 accompanied by a fully vaccinated parent/guardian to mandatory random testing, as of April 1, 2022; (5) exempt cruise ship travellers who, after disembarking, enter Canada by air or land as part of a cruise-related activity from on-arrival testing, as of April 1, 2022; (6) require symptomatic or COVID-19 positive foreign national cruise ship passengers who are permitted to disembark to continue their isolation period, as of April 1, 2022; and (7) ease post-arrival requirements for fully vaccinated travellers, as of April 25, 2022.

act: Canada Student Financial Assistance ActApprentice Loans Act
subject: Regulations Amending the Canada Student Financial Assistance Regulations and the Apprentice Loans Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the CANADA STUDENT FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE REGULATIONS and the APPRENTICE LOANS REGULATIONS in order to (1) increase the Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP) zero payment threshold for family size of one from $25,000 to $40,000; (2) increase RAP zero payment thresholds for other family sizes to align with the thresholds used for Canada Student Grants for Full-Time Students; (3) index all thresholds (including the $40,000 threshold for family size of one) to the Consumer Price Index; (4) reduce the cap on the monthly affordable payment while on RAP from 20% to 10% of a borrower’s family income; and (5) align Apprentice Loan Regulations provisions with the two-year interest waiver legislation.

subject: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Temporary Foreign Workers)
precis: Regulations Amending the IMMIGRATION AND REFUGEE PROTECTION REGULATIONS (TEMPORARY FOREIGN WORKERS) in order to (1) improve worker protections by requiring that an employer provides (i) the most recent information about temporary foreign worker’s (TFW) rights in Canada, (ii) signed employment agreement that outlines the occupation, wages, and working conditions of TFW consistent with those set out in the offer of employment, and (iii) access to healthcare services when TFW becomes injured or ill at the workplace; (2) expand on the definition of “abuse” to include reprisal; (3) prohibit charging or recovering recruitment fees; and (4) authorize certain officers to require documents from third parties to verify employer compliance, reduce timelines to respond to Notices of Preliminary Findings, and create new requirements for Labour Market Impact Assessments.

subject: Regulations Amending the Safe Food for Canadians Regulations

subject: Regulations Amending the Cannabis Regulations (Listing Ingredients for Edible Cannabis)

subject: Regulations Amending the Natural Health Products Regulations

precis: Regulations Amending the SPECIAL IMPORT MEASURES REGULATIONS (SIMR) and the CANADIAN INTERNATIONAL TRADE TRIBUNAL REGULATIONS in order to (1) include the impacts on terms and conditions of employment as factors for the Canadian International Trade Tribunal (CITT) to consider when assessing injury or threat of injury to the domestic industry in both safeguard and anti-dumping and countervailing duty inquiries; (2) amend the SIMR to ensure the CITT and Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) consider impacts on terms and conditions of employment during expiry reviews; (3) amend the SIMR to remove references to “principal cause” in order to provide additional discretion for the CBSA to find circumvention in cases where a change in the trade pattern is caused by the imposition of trade remedy duties, even if it is not the principal cause; and (4) clarify that, in anti-circumvention investigations, the CBSA can consider other factors that could have led to a change in trade patterns that are unrelated to the imposition of trade remedy duties.

subject: Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order
precis: MINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry of foreign nationals, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) continue to exempt travellers who are fully vaccinated, those with a medical contraindication to a vaccine and unvaccinated children less than 12 who are accompanied by fully vaccinated travellers from the requirement to quarantine, as long as they have complied with all applicable measures; (4) continue to maintain all requirements for unvaccinated travellers subject to limited exceptions, to have a valid COVID-19 negative test result before entering Canada, to undergo testing when entering and once again later in the 14-day post-entry period, and to quarantine upon entry into Canada; (5) continue to permit the entry of fully vaccinated foreign nationals arriving for any purpose, as long as they have complied with all applicable measures, and unvaccinated foreign national travellers, if they meet one of the exemptions and are compliant with any applicable measures; (6) remove the additional enhanced measures for fully vaccinated irregular asylum seekers who arrive without a valid pre-arrival test and any unvaccinated accompanying dependants less than 12 years of age; and (7) remove the requirement for those subject to isolation, and who remain in isolation on board a cruise ship for the duration of their time in Canada to obtain permission from a Quarantine Officer to depart Canada

subject: Regulations Amending the Special Economic Measures (Haiti) Regulations

subject: Regulations Amending the Special Economic Measures (Russia) Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the SPECIAL ECONOMIC MEASURES (RUSSIA) REGULATIONS in order to (1) prohibit any person in Canada or any Canadian outside Canada from providing the services listed in the new Schedule, to or for the benefit of Russia or any person in Russia, in relation to the maritime transport of Russian crude oil and petroleum products, unless the oil or petroleum products are purchased at or below the price cap; 2) impose an exception to the service prohibition for transactions involving goods that were loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading prior to December 5, 2022, and unloaded at the port of destination prior to January 19, 2023; (3) impose an exception to the service prohibition for transactions responding to an emergency situation, where implicated services are necessary to ensure navigational safety or to minimize danger to human life or damage to the environment; and (4) impose exceptions to the service prohibition related to the importation of crude oil and petroleum products into the Republic of Bulgaria, the Republic of Croatia, and landlocked European Union Member States.

subject: Regulations Amending the Canadian Aviation Security Regulations, 2012 (Defensive Equipment, Firearms and Ammunition)

subject: Immigration Appeal Division Rules, 2022

subject: Regulations Amending Certain Regulations Made Under the Canada Labour Code (Menstrual Products)

Regulations Amending the CANADIAN AVIATION REGULATIONS (PARTS I, III, IV AND VI TO VIII – AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES) in order to (1) streamline and update terminology to facilitate interpretation of regulatory requirements; (2) eliminate perceived ambiguities and enhance consistency in the interpretation of regulatory requirements; (3) facilitate the adoption and use of innovative technologies; (4) make certain recognized best practices mandatory; (5) facilitate application of procedures in Standard 821 to provide ATC separation; (6) address concerns raised by the SJCSR; and (7) restructure air traffic service provisions.

Regulations Amending the MIGRATORY BIRD SANCTUARY REGULATIONS in order to (1) rename seven Migratory Bird Sanctuaries (MBS) in the Nunavut Settlement Area with Inukitut names identified by the Area Co-Management Committee (ACMC) responsible for each of the MBS; and (2) create a new part XIII to the Schedule for MBS formerly located in the Northwest Territories and now located in Nunavut.

Regulations Amending the WILDLIFE AREA REGULATIONS in order to (1) remove 19 units (1,371.5 ha) from the Wildlife Area Regulations and replace them with five consolidated National Wildlife Areas: Great Sandhills, Harris Sandhills, Longspur, Moose Mountain Creek, and Thickwood Hills; and (2) authorize the following activities within the five new National Wildlife Areas: wildlife viewing; hiking; non-commercial berry picking; and sport hunting.

Regulations Amending the ENERGY EFFICIENCY REGULATIONS, 2016 (AMENDMENT 18) in order to (1) add the following products into the Regulations: air compressors, faucets, line voltage thermostats, pool pumps and showerheads;  (2) expand the scope of what is defined as a general service lamp and introduce or update energy efficiency and testing standards to harmonize with U.S. standards for the following products specifically: air conditioners, heat pumps, gas furnaces, electric water heaters and general service lamps; and (3) expand the use of ambulatory incorporation by reference and update the list of energy-using products that can be amended through Ministerial Regulations for the purpose of maintaining harmonization.

Regulations Amending the SPECIAL ECONOMIC MEASURES (HAITI) REGULATIONS in order to add three (3) individuals who are now subject to a broad dealings ban, to the list of persons under the Regulations in which individuals in Canada, as well as Canadians outside of Canada, are prohibited from dealing in the property of listed persons, entering into transactions with, providing services to them, transferring property to them, or otherwise making goods available them.

Regulations amending the SPECIAL ECONOMIC MEASURES (VENEZUELA) REGULATIONS in order to to add eight (8) individuals to the Schedule of listed persons under the Regulations in which any person in Canada or Canadians outside of Canada are thereby prohibited from dealing in the property of, entering into transactions with, providing services to, transferring property to, or otherwise making goods available to listed persons (individuals and entities).

subject: Order Amending Schedule IX of the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act
precis: Order Amending Schedule IX of the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act in order to expand the import registration requirements for designated devices to also apply to certain component parts suitable for use in pill presses or encapsulators.

subject: Regulations Amending the Pest Control Products Regulations (Class I Medical Devices treated with Antimicrobial Preservatives)
precis: Regulations Amending the Pest Control Products Regulations (Class I Medical Devices treated with Antimicrobial Preservatives) in order to (1) exempt Class I medical devices treated with antimicrobial preservatives from the act; and (2) exempt the antimicrobial preservative itself when it is used as a treatment in such devices.

subject: Fee to be Paid by Foreign Nationals to Participate in an International Youth Exchange Program in Canada Remission Order
precis: Fee to be Paid by Foreign Nationals to Participate in an International Youth Exchange Program in Canada Remission Order in order to remit outstanding debts resulting from the non-collection of the full amount of the annual increases to the International Experience Canada Fee from December 1, 2019, to November 30, 2024.

subject: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (2023 Nova Scotia Floods) Remission Order
precis: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (2023 Nova Scotia Floods) Remission Order in order to remit fees that were waived for Canadians and permanent residents affected by the Nova Scotia floods from July 22 to November 30, 2023.

subject: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (2023 Canada Wildfires) Remission Order
precis: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (2023 Canada Wildfires) Remission Order in order to remit fees that were waived for Canadians and permanent residents affected by the 2023 Canada wildfires from May 6 to November 30, 2023.

subject: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (2025 Canada Wildfires) Remission Order
precis: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (2025 Canada Wildfires) Remission Order in order to remit fees that were waived for Canadians and permanent residents affected by the 2025 Canada wildfires from April 1 to November 30, 2025.

subject: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (2023 Morocco Earthquake) Remission Order

subject: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (2023 Türkiye and Syria Earthquakes) Remission Order
precis: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (2023 Türkiye and Syria Earthquakes) Remission Order in order to remit fees associated with travel documents, citizenship certificates and consular services that were not collected for Canadians and permanent residents of Canada affected by the earthquakes occurring in Türkiye and Syria on February 6, 2023.

subject: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (Iran) Remission Order

subject: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (Haiti) Remission Order
precis: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (Haiti) Remission Order in order to (1) remit fees associated with travel documents, citizenship certificates and consular services that were not collected from Canadians and permanent residents of Canada in Haiti who applied for documents between March 1, 2024, and September 1, 2024; and (2) reimburse fees for overseas temporary resident applicants who left Haiti on or after March 1, 2024, and arrived in Canada on or before April 26, 2024.

subject: Certain Fees in Respect of the Issuance of Identity and Travel Documents (Sudan) Remission Order

subject: Fee Paid or Payable for the Acquisition of Permanent Resident Status (Sudan) Remission Order
precis: Fee Paid or Payable for the Acquisition of Permanent Resident Status (Sudan) Remission Order in order to remit the fee that that was not collected from foreign nationals whose application for permanent residence was approved under public policies.

subject: Fee Paid or Payable for the Acquisition of Permanent Resident Status (Certain Colombian, Haitian and Venezuelan Nationals) Remission Order

subject: Fee Paid or Payable for the Acquisition of Permanent Resident Status (Certain Afghan Nationals) Remission Order

subject: Fee Payable for the Right to be a Citizen Remission Order

subject: Certain Fees Under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations Remission Order

subject: Order Consenting to the Amendments of the Tla’amin Final Agreement
precis: Order consenting to the amendments of the Tla’amin Final Agreement (Treaty) in order to (1) expand jurisdiction in Child and Family Services program delivery; (2) acknowledge that the Treaty is a living agreement and provides a foundation for evolution and an ongoing relationship amongst the Government of Canada, the Government of British Columbia and the Tla’amin Nation; and (3) incorporate specific Tla’amin language terminology throughout the Treaty.

subject: Order Approving the Interim Order Modifying the Operation of Certain Regulations Made Under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999

subject: Agreement on the mutual recognition of professional qualifications for architects
precis: Order authorizing the Minister of Foreign Affairs to take the actions necessary for Decision No 1/2024 of the Joint Committee on Mutual Recognition of Professional Qualifications of 10 October 2024 setting out an agreement on the mutual recognition of professional qualifications for architects to become binding for Canada.

subject: Steel Derivative Goods Surtax Order
precis: Steel Derivative Goods Surtax in order to impose a global surtax of 25 percent on certain goods made with steel such as prefabricated buildings, wire and cable.

subject: Order Amending the Import Control List (2025-2)
precis: Order Amending the Import Control List (2025-2) in order to make consequential changes to ensure the reduced tariff-rate quotas levels are implemented correctly.

subject: Order Amending the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025)
precis: Order Amending the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025) in order to (1) extend relief for public health, public safety and national security entities until June 30, 2026; (2) extend relief for steel goods used in manufacturing, processing, food and beverage packaging and agricultural production to January 31, 2026; and (3) extend relief for aluminum goods used in manufacturing, processing and agricultural production to June 30, 2026; and (4) grant new relief for goods used for the manufacturing of motor vehicles, aerospace goods and related parts starting February 1, 2026, and until June 30, 2026.

subject: Treaty between Canada and Japan on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters
precis: Order authorizing the Prime Minister, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, or a delegate, to sign, on behalf of the Government of Canada, subject to ratification, the Treaty between Canada and Japan on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters.

subject: Prohibition of Certain Toxic Substances Regulations, 2025
precis: Prohibition of Certain Toxic Substances Regulations, 2025 in order to (1) repeal and replace the Prohibition of Certain Toxic Substances Regulations, 2012; (2) restrict the manufacture, use, sale and import of Dechlorane Plus and decabromodiphenyl ethane, and products containing these substances; (3) further restrict the manufacture, use, sale and import of perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS), perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluorocarboxylic acids (LC-PFCAs), hexabromocyclododecane (HBCD) and polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), and products containing these substances; and (4) exempt the transit through Canada of a manufactured item containing a prohibited toxic substance. .

subject: Order Fixing the Day on Which Certain Provisions of the Budget Implementation Act, 2024, No. 1, Come into Force
precis: Order Fixing the Day After the Day on Which this Order is made as the Day on Which Division 4 of Part 4 of the Budget Implementation Act, 2024, No. 1 Come into Force in order to amend the Canada Student Financial Assistance Act and the Canada Student Loans Act that expand the list of occupations eligible for the Canada Student Loan forgiveness benefit.

act:
Canada Student Loans Act
Canada Student Financial Assistance Act
subject: Regulations Amending the Canada Student Loans Regulations and the Canada Student Financial Assistance Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the Canada Student Loans Regulations and the Canada Student Financial Assistance Regulations in order to (1) expand the loan forgiveness benefit to early childhood educators, dentists, dental hygienists, pharmacists, midwives, teachers, social workers, personal support workers, physiotherapists, and psychologists who choose to work in an under-served rural or remote community; and (2) require that applicants provide at least 400 hours of in-person services in the previous year.

subject: Regulations Amending the Small Vessel Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the Small Vessel Regulations in order to (1) introduce a $24 service fee for the issuance, renewal, or transfer of a pleasure craft licences (PCL); (2) establish a five-year validity period for all PCLs, gradually expire lifetime PCLs, expand the Minister’s authority to cancel a PCL for non-compliance; (3) expand the scope of PCL requirements to include wind-powered vessels above six meters in length such as sail-alone vessels; (4) set clearer requirements and timelines for the transfer of PCLs; (5) reduce the timeframe for PCL holders to notify Transport Canada of changes to licence information from 90 days to 30 days; and (6) require vessel manufacturers, builders, and importers to notify Transport Canada of any changes in their contact information within 30 days.

subject: Regulations Amending the PCB Regulations and the Regulations Designating Regulatory Provisions for Purposes of Enforcement (Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999)
precis: Regulations Amending the PCB Regulations and the Regulations Designating Regulatory Provisions for Purposes of Enforcement (Canadian Environment Protection Act, 1999) in order to (1) allow for the continued use and storage of polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB)-containing equipment in nuclear, electrical, and military facilities, as well as museums, subject to certain conditions; (2) clarify that mixing PCB oil with non-PCB oil for the purposes of reducing its concentration is not allowed and, that laboratory tests are not required if the PCB concentration is already known by other means; (3) defer end-of-use deadline for certain PCB-containing electrical equipment to December 31, 2026, or beyond, subject to ministerial approval; and (4) make consequential amendments to certain other regulations to incorporate the provisions of the regulations.

subject: Regulations Amending the Special Economic Measures (Iran) Regulations
precis: Regulations Amending the Special Economic Measures (Iran) Regulations in order to add four (4) individuals to Schedule 1 of the Regulations, prohibiting them from transacting business with individuals and businesses in Canada, and freezing their assets unless otherwise authorized by the Minister of the Foreign Affairs.

subject: Vessel Traffic Services Zone Regulations
precis: Vessel Traffic Services Zone Regulations in order to (1) repeal the Vessel Traffic Services Zones Regulations, the Eastern Canada Vessel Traffic Services Zone Regulations, and the Northern Canada Vessel Traffic Services Zone Regulations, and consolidate their requirements under the new Regulations; (2) standardize reporting requirements across all Canadian vessel traffic services zones; (3) incorporate by reference, on an ambulatory basis, the part of the Radio Aids to Marine Navigation that includes technical details and specifies the data elements and format for vessel reports; (4) make several technical and administrative amendments to standardize terminology and harmonize existing requirements with international standards; (5) amend the Administrative Monetary Penalties and Notices Regulations by designating 26 provisions as violations.

subject: Order Fixing December 15, 2025 as the Day on Which an Act to amend the Citizenship Act (2025)
precis: Order Fixing December 15, 2025 as the Day on Which an Act to amend the Citizenship Act (2025) Comes into Force in order to establish a new framework governing citizenship by descent and provide citizenship to “Lost Canadians” and those impacted by the first-generation limit.

subject: Regulations Amending the Citizenship Regulations (Miscellaneous Program)
precis: Regulations Amending the Citizenship Regulations (Miscellaneous Program) in order to (1) update a reference to specific subsections of the Citizenship Regulations No.2; (2) correct a discrepancy between English and French versions; and (3) clarify that applications to renounce citizenship can be made by minors.

subject: Order Repealing Certain Regulations made Under the Railway Safety Act

subject: Landfill Methane Regulations

subject: Regulations Amending the Regulations Respecting Reduction in the Release of Methane and Certain Volatile Organic Compounds (Upstream Oil and Gas Sector)

subject: Regulations Amending the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations (Canadian Update)

subject: Regulations Amending the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (Seizure and Facilities for Holding and Examination —Miscellaneous Program)

act: Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Act
